nodes.title: Modular symbols
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and a right ℤ[Γ]-module V, Symb_Γ(V) is the group of additive maps φ : Δ₀ → V with φ(γD) = φ(D)|γ^{-1} for all γ ∈ Γ, D ∈ Δ₀, where Δ₀ = Div⁰(P¹(ℚ)) is the degree-zero divisor module with its action of GL₂⁺(ℚ) by linear fractional transformations (imported from ModularForms Layer 8, see requests). In the formal version V carries the left representation ρ(γ)v = v|γ^{-1}, and the condition reads φ(γD) = ρ(γ)φ(D); equivalently Symb_Γ(V) = Hom_{ℤ[Γ]}(Δ₀, V).
hypotheses: Γ acts on Δ₀ through SL₂(ℤ) → GL₂(ℚ).
Left/right conventions: Pollack–Stevens' right action v|γ is recorded as the left representation v ↦ v|γ^{-1}.
proofSteps: Define symbols Γ ρ as the additive subgroup of maps Δ₀ → V satisfying the equivariance; closure under sums and negatives is immediate.
A modular symbol is determined by its values on the unimodular divisors {γ0} − {γ∞}, because these generate Δ₀ (Manin's theorem, imported from ModularForms Layer 8).
acceptance: Symb_{SL₂(ℤ)}(ℤ) = 0: by the Manin relations φ({0} − {∞}) = v satisfies 2v = 0 and 3v = 0.
Symb_{Γ₀(11)}(ℤ) has rank 3 = 2g + (c − 1), with genus g = 1 and c = 2 cusps.
When the orders of torsion elements act invertibly on V, Symb_Γ(V) ≅ H¹_c(H/Γ, Ṽ) (Pollack–Stevens, citing Ash–Stevens [2, Prop. 4.2]); planned as remaining work.

nodes.title: ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] is free over ℤ[Γ]
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ G of finite index in a group G (here G = SL₂(ℤ) or PSL₂(ℤ)), ℤ[G] is a free left ℤ[Γ]-module with basis any set of right coset representatives {g_j} of Γ\G; consequently Hom_{ℤ[Γ]}(ℤ[G], V) ≅ ∏_j V by F ↦ (F(g_j))_j.
hypotheses: Γ acts by left multiplication through the inclusion.
proofSteps: SL₂(ℤ) = ⊔_i Γ g_i gives ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] = ⊕_i ℤ[Γ]g_i, and γ g_i ↦ (γ, i) is a bijection Γ × (Γ\SL₂(ℤ)) → SL₂(ℤ).
acceptance: For finite index the basis is finite, of size [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ].
Combined with the Manin relations this gives the ℤ[Γ]-presentation of Δ₀ by coset generators.

nodes.title: The coefficient modules V_k = Sym^k
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R and k ≥ 0, V_k(R) is the R-module of homogeneous polynomials of degree k in X, Y, with the right action of integral matrices of nonzero determinant (P|γ)(X, Y) = P((X, Y)·γ*) = P(dX − cY, −bX + aY) for γ = (a b; c d), γ* its adjugate; restricted to Γ it gives the left representation γ ↦ (P ↦ P|γ^{-1}).
hypotheses: The adjugate keeps the action integral, so it is defined for the monoid of integral matrices, not only GL₂(ℚ).

The row-adjugate right action differs from current Tau Ceti’s column-adjugate left action: slashVk(γ)=binaryFormAdjugateRep(γ.transpose) on the same homogeneous polynomial module. Current BinaryForms is a reuse boundary; this transposition dictionary, not a duplicate polynomial carrier, is the new task.
proofSteps: V_k(R) := MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) R k; P|γ := aeval of the substitution X ↦ dX − cY, Y ↦ −bX + aY, which preserves degree k.
Right action: (γδ)* = δ*γ* gives P|(γδ) = (P|γ)|δ.
acceptance: For nontrivial R, rank V_k(R)=k+1; the zero ring is excluded from this rank assertion.
A scalar matrix c·1 acts by c^k.
V_0 is the trivial representation; Pollack–Stevens use V_k = Sym^k(ℚ_p²) with the same formula.

nodes.statement: Σ₀(N) is the monoid of integral matrices (a b; c d) with nonzero determinant, N | c and (a, N) = 1; it contains Γ₀(N) and the matrices (ℓ 0; 0 1) for (ℓ, N) = 1 and (1 a; 0 ℓ) for all a, ℓ ≥ 1.
proofSteps: Closure: the lower-left entry of a product is c a′ + d c′ ≡ 0 mod N, and the upper-left entry a a′ + b c′ ≡ a a′ mod N is prime to N; determinants multiply.
acceptance: Γ₀(N) ⊆ Σ₀(N) (Gamma0_le_Sigma0).
(1 a; 0 ℓ) ∈ Σ₀(N) for every a and ℓ ≥ 1; (ℓ 0; 0 1) ∈ Σ₀(N) iff (ℓ, N) = 1.
This is Pollack–Stevens' S₀(p) with p replaced by N.

nodes.title: Hecke operators on modular symbols
nodes.statement: For V with a right Σ₀(N)-action extending its Γ₀(N)-action, and φ ∈ Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V): (φ|δ)(D) := φ(δD)|δ; for a prime ℓ ∤ N, φ|T_ℓ := φ|(ℓ 0; 0 1) + Σ_{a=0}^{ℓ−1} φ|(1 a; 0 ℓ); for q | N, φ|U_q := Σ_{a=0}^{q−1} φ|(1 a; 0 q). These preserve Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V) and commute.
hypotheses: V's Γ₀(N)-action is the restriction of the Σ₀(N)-action.

The suggested coefficient action is a monoid homomorphism from the opposite matrix semigroup to module endomorphisms, and its restriction is ρ(γ⁻¹). Preservation and commutativity apply to equivariant symbols, not arbitrary divisor maps.
proofSteps: The listed matrices are representatives of Γ₀(N)\Γ₀(N)(ℓ 0; 0 1)Γ₀(N) (resp. for U_q); right multiplication by γ ∈ Γ₀(N) permutes the cosets, so Σ φ|α_i is again Γ₀(N)-invariant.

The operators come from an action of the Γ₀(N) Hecke ring of double cosets on Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V), with T_ℓ the class of Γ₀(N)(ℓ 0; 0 1)Γ₀(N); commutativity follows from commutativity of that ring (Tau Ceti HeckeRing.GL2.commSemiringHeckeRingGamma0).
acceptance: On Symb_{Γ₀(11)}(ℤ), T_2 has characteristic polynomial (x − 3)(x + 2)²: eigenvalue 3 on the boundary (Eisenstein) part and a₂(11a) = −2 on the plus and minus parts.

nodes.statement: If ι normalises Γ and 2 acts invertibly on V, then Symb_Γ(V) = Symb_Γ(V)^+ ⊕ Symb_Γ(V)^− into ±1-eigenspaces of ι, via φ = (φ + φ|ι)/2 + (φ − φ|ι)/2; the decomposition is preserved by the Hecke operators when ι commutes with them.

proofSteps: The idempotents (1 ± ι)/2 are defined since 2 is invertible and ι² = 1.

nodes.title: Modular symbols as functions on cosets (Manin symbols, cohomological side)
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, let {g_j} be right coset representatives of Γ\SL₂(ℤ), and let V be a right ℤ[Γ]-module. For g ∈ SL₂(ℤ) write g = γ_g g_{j(g)} with γ_g ∈ Γ. The map φ ↦ (v_j)_j, v_j := φ({g_j 0} − {g_j ∞}), is an isomorphism from Symb_Γ(V) onto the families (v_j) ∈ ∏_j V such that, for every j, with x(g) := v_{j(g)}|γ_g^{-1}: x(g_j) + x(g_j σ) = 0, x(g_j) + x(g_j τ) + x(g_j τ²) = 0, and x(g_j) = x(−g_j), where σ = (0 −1; 1 0) and τ = (0 −1; 1 −1).
hypotheses: Γ has finite index in SL₂(ℤ).
The relation list is the image of Manin's kernel ℤ[G](1 + σ) + ℤ[G](1 + τ + τ²) + ℤ[G](1 − (−1)) under the coset basis.
proofSteps: By Manin's theorem (requested from ModularForms Layer 8) d : ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] → Δ₀, g ↦ {g0} − {g∞}, is surjective with kernel the left ideal I generated by 1 + σ, 1 + τ + τ² and 1 − (−1); so Symb_Γ(V) = Hom_{ℤ[Γ]}(ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)]/I, V).
A ℤ[Γ]-linear map F : ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] → V is determined by the values F(g_j) on the coset basis (coset-basis), with F(γ g_j) = F(g_j)|γ^{-1}.
F kills I iff F(g(1 + σ)) = F(g(1 + τ + τ²)) = F(g(1 − (−1))) = 0 for every g; by Γ-equivariance it suffices to take g = g_j, and F(g) = x(g) by the first step.
Hence evaluation at the unimodular divisors d(g_j) identifies Symb_Γ(V) with the stated set of families.
acceptance: For Γ = SL₂(ℤ) (one coset, g₁ = 1) and V = ℤ with trivial action the conditions read 2v = 0 and 3v = 0, so Symb_{SL₂(ℤ)}(ℤ) = 0.
For Γ = Γ₀(11) (12 cosets) and V = ℤ the solution module has rank 3, matching Pollack's worked Γ₀(11) example.
Changing the coset representatives changes the isomorphism by the corresponding γ-twists and not its image.

nodes.title: A modular symbol is determined by its values on the fundamental-domain generators
nodes.statement: Let Γ ⊊ PSL₂(ℤ) have finite index and contain T = (1 1; 0 1), and let D₁, …, D_t, D_∞, D′₁, …, D′_s, D″₁, …, D″_r be the generators of Δ₀ read off a Farey fundamental domain, with the matrices γ_i, γ′_i (order 2) and γ″_i (order 3) in Γ (Pollack–Stevens §§2.4–2.5; the presentation is imported from ModularForms Layer 8). For a right Γ-module V and v₁, …, v_t, v_∞, v′₁, …, v′_s, v″₁, …, v″_r ∈ V with v_∞|Δ = Σ_i v_i|(1 − γ_i) − Σ_i v′_i − Σ_i v″_i (Δ := T − 1), v′_i|(1 + γ′_i) = 0 and v″_i|(1 + γ″_i + γ″_i²) = 0, there is a unique φ ∈ Symb_Γ(V) with φ(D_i) = v_i, φ(D_∞) = v_∞, φ(D′_i) = v′_i and φ(D″_i) = v″_i; every φ arises so. This is Pollack–Stevens' Corollaries 2.7 and 2.10 with the sign of the D_∞ relation corrected (sourceIssues E1).
hypotheses: Γ has finite index in PSL₂(ℤ), contains T and is proper (for the three-torsion version); for Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) apply it to the image Γ̄ and to V^{⟨−1⟩∩Γ}, since −1 acts trivially on Δ₀.
The relations among the generators are Σ_i (γ_i^{-1} − 1)D_i + Σ_i D′_i + Σ_i D″_i = (1 − T^{-1})D_∞, (1 + γ′_i)D′_i = 0 and (1 + γ″_i + γ″_i²)D″_i = 0.
proofSteps: Theorem 2.6/2.9 of Pollack–Stevens, as corrected (request to ModularForms Layer 8): Δ₀ is generated over ℤ[Γ] by the D's with the displayed relations. The relation is derived from the printed boundary relation (1 − T^{-1})e_∞ + Σ(1 − γ_i^{-1})e_i + Σ e′_i ∈ J on p. 11 by applying ∂, with D′_i = −∂(e′_i).
A ℤ[Γ]-linear map out of a presented module is the same as values on the generators satisfying the relations.

Apply φ(γD) = φ(D)|γ^{-1} to the first relation: Σ v_i|(γ_i − 1) + Σ v′_i + Σ v″_i = v_∞ − v_∞|T = −v_∞|Δ; the torsion relations give v′_i|(1 + γ′_i) = 0 and v″_i|(1 + γ″_i + γ″_i²) = 0 because γ′_i, γ″_i have order 2, 3 in PSL₂(ℤ).
acceptance: Γ₀(2) (t = 0, s = 1, F the ideal triangle with vertices −1, 0, ∞, γ′₁ = (1 1; −2 −1)): D′₁ = (1 − T^{-1})D_∞ = {0} − {−1}; with the printed sign the relation would force 2D′₁ = 0 in the torsion-free Δ₀.
Γ₀(11) with V = V_k: the relation matches Pollack's worked example (1 − (1 −1; 0 1))({0} − {∞}) + Σ(1 − γ)D = 0 (AWS notes, footnote 10), whose γ is Pollack–Stevens' γ_i^{-1}.
For V = ℚ with trivial action the conditions reduce to Σ_i v′_i + Σ_i v″_i = 0 and v′_i = v″_i = 0 (2, 3 invertible), so dim Symb_Γ(ℚ) = t + 1.

nodes.title: Boundary symbols
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and a right ℤ[Γ]-module V, BSymb_Γ(V) := Hom_{ℤ[Γ]}(ℤ[P¹(ℚ)], V), the maps ψ : P¹(ℚ) → V with ψ(γc) = ψ(c)|γ^{-1}. Restriction along Δ₀ ⊆ ℤ[P¹(ℚ)] gives res : BSymb_Γ(V) → Symb_Γ(V), whose image Eis_Γ(V) is the module of Eisenstein (boundary) symbols. Choosing representatives c₁, …, c_ν of the finitely many cusps Γ\P¹(ℚ) gives BSymb_Γ(V) ≅ ⊕_j V^{Γ_{c_j}}, ψ ↦ (ψ(c_j))_j, where Γ_c is the stabiliser of c.
hypotheses: Γ has finite index, so Γ\P¹(ℚ) is finite (P¹(ℚ) = SL₂(ℤ)/⟨±T⟩ as an SL₂(ℤ)-set).
V^{Γ_c} is the invariants for the right action, v|γ = v for γ ∈ Γ_c.
proofSteps: ℤ[P¹(ℚ)] = ⊕_j ℤ[Γ/Γ_{c_j}] as a left ℤ[Γ]-module, since P¹(ℚ) is the disjoint union of the orbits Γc_j ≅ Γ/Γ_{c_j}.
Hom_{ℤ[Γ]}(ℤ[Γ/H], V) ≅ V^H for H ≤ Γ (Frobenius reciprocity for permutation modules), giving the cusp description.
res is ℤ-linear and Γ-compatible because Δ₀ is a ℤ[Γ]-submodule of ℤ[P¹(ℚ)].
acceptance: For Γ = SL₂(ℤ) and V = ℤ (one cusp, stabiliser ⟨±T⟩), BSymb ≅ ℤ consists of the constant functions and res = 0.
For Γ₀(p), p prime, there are two cusps ∞ and 0 and BSymb_{Γ₀(p)}(ℤ) ≅ ℤ².
Eis_Γ(V) is stable under the Hecke operators of hecke-operators.

nodes.title: The map from modular symbols to group cohomology
nodes.statement: For φ ∈ Symb_Γ(V) (V with the left representation ρ(γ)v = v|γ^{-1}) and a base cusp x ∈ P¹(ℚ), c_φ(γ) := φ({γx} − {x}) is a 1-cocycle of Γ with values in (V, ρ); its class δ(φ) ∈ H¹(Γ, V) does not depend on x, and δ : Symb_Γ(V) → H¹(Γ, V) is ℤ-linear. Up to sign δ is the connecting homomorphism of Hom_Γ(−, V) applied to 0 → Δ₀ → ℤ[P¹(ℚ)] → ℤ → 0.
hypotheses: Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index; V a right ℤ[Γ]-module, equivalently the left representation ρ.
H¹(Γ, V) is Mathlib's groupCohomology of the representation (V, ρ) in degree 1.
proofSteps: Cocycle identity: c_φ(γη) = φ({γηx} − {γx}) + φ({γx} − {x}) = ρ(γ)c_φ(η) + c_φ(γ).
Base change x ↦ y changes c_φ by the coboundary γ ↦ (ρ(γ) − 1)φ({y} − {x}).

For the abstract contravariant connecting-map interpretation, extend φ to F({c})=φ({c}−{x}); its failure of equivariance is the degree times −c_φ. The formal construction uses the explicit native 1-cocycle and H1 quotient, not groupCohomology.δ, which is covariant in a short exact coefficient sequence.
acceptance: For V = ℂ trivial, Γ = Γ₀(N) and φ = ψ_f of a weight-two cusp form, δ(φ) is the homomorphism γ ↦ 2πi ∫_x^{γx} f(z) dz.
δ kills Eis_Γ(V): for φ = res(ψ), c_φ(γ) = ψ(γx) − ψ(x) = (ρ(γ) − 1)ψ(x) is a coboundary.
δ is compatible with the Hecke operators defined on H¹ by double cosets (Wiese Definition 7.21).

nodes.title: The boundary exact sequence for modular symbols
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and any right ℤ[Γ]-module V the sequence 0 → V^Γ → BSymb_Γ(V) → Symb_Γ(V) → H¹(Γ, V) → ⊕_{c ∈ Γ\P¹(ℚ)} H¹(Γ_c, V) is exact, where the first map sends v to the constant function, the second is res, the third is δ (symbols-to-cohomology) and the last is the product of the restrictions to the cusp stabilisers (choosing representatives).
hypotheses: No invertibility hypothesis: the sequence is exact integrally.
The cusp stabilisers Γ_c are the conjugates of Γ ∩ ⟨±T⟩, cyclic modulo ±1.
proofSteps: Constants inject into boundary functions, and a boundary function restricts to zero on Δ₀ exactly when it is constant; equivariance makes that constant Γ-invariant.

If c_φ(g)=(ρ(g)−1)v, the function F(c)=φ({c}−{x})+v is Γ-equivariant and extends φ. Conversely the restriction of any boundary function has a coboundary cocycle. This proves exactness at symbols directly over ℤ.
At a cusp r fixed by h, change the cocycle base point from x to r; its restriction is zero there. Thus δ takes values in parabolic cohomology.

For a parabolic cocycle c choose one representative r per cusp orbit and v_r with c(h)=(ρ(h)−1)v_r for h∈Γ_r. Put F(gr)=c(g)−ρ(g)v_r. The stabilizer identity makes F well defined and gives F(gx)=ρ(g)F(x)+c(g). Differences φ({b}−{a})=F(b)−F(a) are an equivariant symbol, and c_φ differs from c by a coboundary. This proves exactness at H¹ without an unimplemented first-variable Ext/Shapiro interface.
acceptance: Γ = Γ₀(11), V = ℚ: 0 → ℚ → ℚ² → ℚ³ → ℚ³ → ℚ², with H¹(Γ₀(11), ℚ) = Hom(Γ₀(11), ℚ) of dimension 3 = 2g + (c − 1) (the image of Γ₀(11) in PSL₂(ℤ) is free of rank 3), Eis of dimension 1 and image of δ the 2-dimensional parabolic part.
For V with V^{Γ_c} = 0 at every cusp the boundary terms vanish and Symb_Γ(V) ↪ H¹(Γ, V).
Exactness at Symb_Γ(V): ker δ = Eis_Γ(V).

Independence of representatives: restriction to Γ_{γc} = γΓ_cγ^{-1} is restriction to Γ_c composed with conjugation by γ, an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Modular symbols modulo Eisenstein symbols are parabolic cohomology
nodes.statement: δ induces an isomorphism Symb_Γ(V)/Eis_Γ(V) ≅ H¹_par(Γ, V), compatible with the Hecke operators, the diamond operators and ι.
hypotheses: Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index; any right ℤ[Γ]-module V; no invertibility hypothesis.
proofSteps: By symbols-cohomology-sequence, ker δ = Eis_Γ(V) and the image of δ is the kernel of the restriction to the cusp stabilisers, which is H¹_par(Γ, V).
Hecke compatibility: δ commutes with T (symbols-to-cohomology API), and Eis_Γ(V) is Hecke-stable (boundary-symbols API).

nodes.title: Descent of modular symbols from a normal subgroup
nodes.statement: Let Γ′ ⊴ Γ be finite-index subgroups of SL₂(ℤ) and V a right ℤ[Γ]-module. Then Γ/Γ′ acts on Symb_{Γ′}(V) by φ ↦ φ|γ, and Symb_Γ(V) = Symb_{Γ′}(V)^{Γ/Γ′}, integrally and with no division. If [Γ : Γ′] is invertible on V, then restriction gives H¹(Γ, V) ≅ H¹(Γ′, V)^{Γ/Γ′} and H¹_par(Γ, V) ≅ H¹_par(Γ′, V)^{Γ/Γ′}, and Symb_Γ(V) is a direct summand of Symb_{Γ′}(V) via the averaging idempotent e = [Γ:Γ′]^{-1} Σ_{γ ∈ Γ/Γ′} (·)|γ.
hypotheses: Γ′ is normal in Γ of finite index. Use Γ′=Γ∩Γ(M) with M≥5, since Γ(M) is a normal reduction kernel, is torsion-free and has only regular cusps. The intersection retains these properties. Γ∩Γ₁(M) is not generally normal in Γ.
Only the second and third statements use that [Γ : Γ′] is invertible; the first holds over ℤ. Dividing by the order of an elliptic stabiliser is never used.
proofSteps: (φ|γ)(D) = φ(γD)|γ is well defined on Symb_{Γ′}(V) because Γ′ is normal, and Γ′ acts trivially; a Γ′-symbol fixed by all of Γ is a Γ-symbol, and conversely.

Construct degree-one corestriction by a finite coset transversal (decompose each translated representative into a subgroup element and another representative, apply the cocycle, and sum the coefficient translates). Check that it takes cocycles and coboundaries to cocycles and coboundaries, and that cor∘res=[Γ:Γ′] and res∘cor=Σ_{Γ/Γ′} conjugation on H¹. Dividing by the index gives injectivity and surjectivity onto invariants. These transfer identities are new proof obligations inside this target, not provided by H1InfRes_exact. That pinned theorem supplies only exactness of the first three inflation/restriction terms.

Restrict the transfer to each cusp using the double-coset decomposition: subgroup parabolic classes give zero in every cusp term. Conversely restriction to Γ′∩Γ_c is injective on H¹(Γ_c,V), because its finite index divides [Γ:Γ′] and is invertible. Hence the global restriction isomorphism identifies parabolic subspaces.
e is an idempotent onto the invariants when [Γ : Γ′] is invertible.
acceptance: Γ = Γ₀(N), Γ′ = Γ₁(N): Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V) = Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V)^{(ℤ/N)^×} for the diamond action.
Γ = SL₂(ℤ), Γ′ = Γ(4) (normal and torsion-free): Symb_{SL₂(ℤ)}(V_k(ℤ)) = Symb_{Γ(4)}(V_k(ℤ))^{SL₂(ℤ)/Γ(4)} over ℤ, with no division by 2 or 3.

nodes.title: Diamond operators on modular symbols
nodes.statement: Let V be a right ℤ[Γ₀(N)]-module (for instance the restriction of a right Σ₀(N)-module). For d ∈ (ℤ/N)^× choose σ_d ∈ Γ₀(N) whose lower-right entry is ≡ d mod N, and put ⟨d⟩φ := φ|σ_d, i.e. (⟨d⟩φ)(D) = φ(σ_d D)|σ_d, for φ ∈ Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V). This is independent of the choice of σ_d, defines a homomorphism (ℤ/N)^× → Aut(Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V)), and commutes with T_ℓ (ℓ ∤ N), U_q (q | N) when the coefficient action extends to their Hecke monoid, and with ι when it extends compatibly to the infinity involution.
hypotheses: Γ₁(N) ⊴ Γ₀(N) with Γ₀(N)/Γ₁(N) ≅ (ℤ/N)^× via the lower-right entry (Mathlib's Gamma0Map).
Convention: the lower-right entry d, as in Tau Ceti's diamondOp on forms; with the upper-left entry one gets ⟨d^{-1}⟩.

The diamond construction itself requires only Γ₀(N)-coefficients. Each Hecke or involution compatibility additionally requires the corresponding coefficient action and its group/monoid relations, as for V_k or weight-k distributions.
proofSteps: Well defined: two choices differ by an element of Γ₁(N), which fixes every Γ₁(N)-symbol.
Multiplicativity: σ_d σ_e has lower-right entry ≡ de, and φ|(σ_dσ_e) = (φ|σ_d)|σ_e; the group is abelian, so the order does not matter.
Commutation with T_ℓ and U_q: the double cosets Γ₁(N)(1 0; 0 ℓ)Γ₁(N) are normalised by Γ₀(N); commutation with ι: ι σ_d ι has the same lower-right entry.
acceptance: ⟨1⟩=id and ⟨−1⟩ acts by (−1)^k on polynomial-coefficient symbols. For odd k over characteristic zero, equality with id forces the symbol space to be zero; the zero space is not a counterexample to the scalar-action formula.
Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V)^{⟨·⟩} = Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V) (symbols-level-descent).
Under the period-symbol map, ⟨d⟩ψ_f = ψ_{⟨d⟩f} with Tau Ceti's diamondOp on S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N)).

nodes.title: Hecke operators on Γ₁(N)-symbols
nodes.statement: For V a right module over Σ₀(N) (or a submonoid containing Γ₀(N) and every displayed good- and bad-prime representative), and φ ∈ Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V): for a prime ℓ ∤ N, φ|T_ℓ := Σ_{a=0}^{ℓ−1} φ|(1 a; 0 ℓ) + φ|σ_ℓ(ℓ 0; 0 1), and for q | N, φ|U_q := Σ_{a=0}^{q−1} φ|(1 a; 0 q). These preserve Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V), commute with each other and with the diamond operators, and restrict to the Γ₀(N) operators of hecke-operators on Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V).
hypotheses: σ_ℓ ∈ Γ₀(N) has lower-right entry ≡ ℓ mod N (so σ_ℓ(ℓ 0; 0 1) ∈ Δ¹ₗ(N)), as in the double-coset decomposition Δ^ℓ_1(N) = ⊔ Γ₁(N)σ_a(a b; 0 d).

nodes.title: Modular symbols with character
nodes.statement: For a ring R, a right R[Γ₀(N)]-module V and a character ε : (ℤ/N)^× → R^×, Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V)[ε] := {φ : ⟨d⟩φ = ε(d)φ for all d}. Equivalently it is Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V ⊗ R_{ε}), where R_{ε} is R with the right Γ₀(N)-action r·γ = ε(d_γ)^{-1}r (d_γ the lower-right entry).
hypotheses: For polynomial coefficients every φ in the ε-space satisfies (ε(−1)−(−1)^k)φ=0. This forces the space to vanish if that scalar is a unit; in particular it does so over a field of characteristic not two with mismatched parity. In an arbitrary ring, distinct values and invertibility of 2 alone do not suffice.
The twist uses the lower-right entry and ε^{-1}, matching the diamond convention of diamond-operators.
Hecke/involution stability assumes that the Γ₀(N)-coefficient action extends compatibly to the relevant Hecke monoid and infinity involution.

The eigenspace is a Hecke-stable submodule because the diamond operators commute with T_ℓ and U_q.

nodes.title: The character decomposition of Γ₁(N)-symbols
nodes.statement: Put G=(ℤ/N)^× and m=|G|. Let B=ℤ[1/m,ζ_m] with a chosen primitive m-th root in characteristic zero, and let R be a commutative B-algebra. Index by the m ordinary characters of G valued in B, transported to R. Then Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V)=⊕_ε Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V)[ε] as an internal direct sum. This includes characteristic-zero splitting fields and B itself. The decomposition is compatible with Hecke and infinity operators when their coefficient actions exist. It is not indexed by all possible R-valued characters when R has idempotents.
hypotheses: The specified character system is the one inherited from B. Its orthogonality identities and m invertibility survive base change to R. Merely saying that a ring contains all character values is insufficient: a product ring can have additional mixed characters.

e_ε projects onto the ε-eigenspace of the diamond action; they commute with Hecke operators and ι.

nodes.title: Hom-side symbols are the dual of homological symbols
nodes.statement: For finite-index Γ, a left ℤ[Γ]-module W, and an abelian group M with trivial action, give Hom_ℤ(W, M) the right action (f|γ)(w) = f(γw). Then Symb_Γ(Hom_ℤ(W, M)) ≅ Hom_ℤ((Δ₀ ⊗ W)_Γ, M), φ ↦ ([D ⊗ w] ↦ φ(D)(w)), naturally in W and M. If W is a left module over a monoid Σ ⊇ Γ (Σ₀(N), Σ₁(N) or GL₂⁺(ℚ) ∩ M₂(ℤ)), the Hecke operator Σ_i φ|δ_i corresponds to precomposition with the operator [D ⊗ w] ↦ Σ_i [δ_i D ⊗ δ_i w] on the coinvariants, and likewise for ⟨d⟩ and ι. With W = Sym^{k}(ℤ²) this identifies Symb_Γ(Hom(Sym^k ℤ², M)) with the ℤ-dual (with values in M) of ModularForms Layer 8's module 𝕄, transposing its Hecke operators.
hypotheses: (Δ₀ ⊗ W)_Γ is the Γ-coinvariants of the diagonal action; Layer 8 uses Γ = Γ₁(N) and W = Sym^{k−2}(ℤ²).
The Hecke identification needs the same coset representatives δ_i on both sides; the transpose reverses composition, and commutativity of the Hecke algebra makes this harmless.
proofSteps: Tensor–hom adjunction: Hom_ℤ(Δ₀ ⊗ W, M) ≅ Hom_ℤ(Δ₀, Hom_ℤ(W, M)).
Γ-invariant maps on the left correspond to Γ-equivariant maps on the right (coinvariants are left adjoint to the trivial-module functor, Rep.coinvariantsAdjunction; Rep.coinvariantsTensor).
For the Hecke operators, (φ|δ)(D)(w) = (φ(δD)|δ)(w) = φ(δD)(δw), so φ|T evaluated on [D ⊗ w] is φ evaluated on Σ_i [δ_iD ⊗ δ_iw].

For Γ₀(11), W = ℤ: rank (Δ₀)_Γ = 3 = rank Symb_{Γ₀(11)}(ℤ).

nodes.title: The invariant pairing between V_k and Sym^k
nodes.statement: Let W_k(R) = R[X, Y]_k with the left action (γ·Q)(X, Y) = Q((X, Y)γ) and V_k(R) the same module with the right action (P|γ)(X, Y) = P((X, Y)γ*), γ* = adj γ (polynomial-coefficients). If k! is invertible in R there is a unique R-bilinear pairing ⟨ , ⟩ : V_k(R) × W_k(R) → R with ⟨(uX + vY)^k, (sX + tY)^k⟩ = (ut − vs)^k for all u, v, s, t ∈ R; on monomials ⟨X^iY^{k−i}, X^jY^{k−j}⟩ = (−1)^{k−i}/C(k, i) if i + j = k and 0 otherwise. It is perfect and satisfies ⟨P|γ, Q⟩ = ⟨P, γ·Q⟩ for every integral γ with det γ ≠ 0; so P ↦ ⟨P, ·⟩ is an isomorphism of right modules V_k(R) ≅ Hom_R(W_k(R), R). Over ℤ the pairing takes values in ℤ[1/k!] and is not integral for k ≥ 2.
hypotheses: k! ∈ R^× for the pairing to exist on all of V_k(R) × W_k(R); no determinant twist appears.
The integral comparison of Symb_Γ(V_k(ℤ)) with Hom(𝕄, ℤ) goes through the divided-power lattice and belongs to L1's integral-lattice work.
proofSteps: Write ℓ_a(X, Y) = a₁X + a₂Y; then P|γ turns ℓ_a^k into ℓ_{γ*a}^k and γ·Q turns ℓ_b^k into ℓ_{γb}^k.
det(γ*a | b) = det(γ*)·det(a | γ*^{-1}b) = det γ · det(a | γb)/det γ = det(a | γb), so the formula is invariant.

Expanding both sides in monomials forces ⟨X^iY^{k−i}, X^{k−i}Y^{i}⟩·C(k, i)² = C(k, i)(−1)^{k−i}, giving the stated values; they span when k! is invertible, and the matrix is anti-diagonal with unit entries, so the pairing is perfect.
acceptance: k = 1: ⟨uX + vY, sX + tY⟩ = ut − vs, the determinant pairing.
k = 2: ⟨XY, XY⟩ = −1/2, so the pairing is not integral.
Invariance check with γ = (1 1; 0 1), k = 2, P = X², Q = Y².

nodes.title: The period symbol of a cusp form
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 0, Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and f ∈ S_{k+2}(Γ), ψ_f : Δ₀ → V_k(ℂ) is the additive map with ψ_f({s} − {r}) = 2πi ∫_r^s f(z)(zX + Y)^k dz (geodesic path in H, improper at cusps). Then ψ_f ∈ Symb_Γ(V_k(ℂ)), f ↦ ψ_f is ℂ-linear, ψ_{f|δ} relates to ψ_f|δ for the weight-(k+2) slash action f|δ = det(δ)^{k+1}(cz + d)^{−k−2}f(δz), so ψ_{T f} = ψ_f|T for T_ℓ, U_q and ⟨d⟩. Under polynomial-duality and symbols-coinvariants-duality, ⟨ψ_f(D), Q⟩ = 2πi · periodMap′(f)(D ⊗ w·Q) with w = (0 1; −1 0), i.e. ψ_f is Layer 8's period map transported to the Hom side.
hypotheses: Convergence at cusps: f is a cusp form (exponential decay at every cusp); this analytic input is Layer 8's convergence milestone.
Orientation: {s} − {r} is the path from r to s; Layer 8's rawPairing integrates {α, β} from β to α.
proofSteps: Well defined on Δ₀: additivity over paths (path independence of holomorphic integrals in H) makes the value on {s} − {r} consistent with the relations of Δ₀.

Hecke equivariance: the same substitution for δ ∈ Σ₀(N) gives ψ_{f|δ}(D) = ψ_f(δD)|δ; summing over coset representatives.

Comparison with Layer 8: ⟨(zX + Y)^k, Q⟩ = (w·Q)(z, 1) with w = (0 1; −1 0), as one checks on Q = (sX + tY)^k where both sides equal (tz − s)^k; so pairing ψ_f with Q is 2πi times Layer 8's rawPairing on D ⊗ w·Q.

nodes.title: Dimension of parabolic cohomology
nodes.statement: Let K have characteristic zero and Γ≤SL₂(ℤ) have finite index and trivial stabilizers on H. Write μ=[PSL₂(ℤ):Γ̄], and c_k=Σ_{r∈Γ\P¹(ℚ)} dim_K V_k(K)^{Γ_r}. Then dim H¹(Γ,V_k)=(k+1)μ/6+δ_{k,0}, and dim H¹_par(Γ,V_k)=(k+1)μ/6−c_k+2δ_{k,0}. A regular cusp has a positive unipotent stabilizer generator and contributes one. An irregular cusp has a negative unipotent generator and contributes one for even k and zero for odd k. Thus c_k is all cusps for even k and regular cusps for odd k.
hypotheses: Γ is torsion-free as an SL₂(ℤ) subgroup (in particular −1∉Γ). The index μ is that of its image in PSL₂(ℤ), not its index in SL₂(ℤ).
Characteristic zero; the invariants/coinvariants computations use the nonzero cusp width and k! as units. This allows both regular and irregular cusp lifts.
proofSteps: M = Coind_Γ^{PSL₂(ℤ)} V_k(K) has dimension (k + 1)μ; H¹(Γ, V_k) = H¹(PSL₂(ℤ), M) (Shapiro).
Mayer–Vietoris for PSL₂(ℤ) = ⟨σ⟩ ∗ ⟨τ⟩: 0 → M^G → M^{⟨σ⟩} ⊕ M^{⟨τ⟩} → M → H¹(G, M) → 0, with M^{⟨σ⟩} and M^{⟨τ⟩} of dimensions μ(k+1)/2 and μ(k+1)/3 when the stabilisers are trivial.

Finite index ensures Γ contains powers of both upper and lower unipotents, so dim V_k^Γ=dim (V_k)_Γ=δ_{k,0}. At a regular cusp T^w, invariants and H¹=coinvariants both have dimension one. At an irregular cusp −T^w the action on degree k is (−1)^k times a unipotent: for odd k, the operator (−T^w)−1 is invertible, so both dimensions vanish.
Combine with the exact row 0 → H¹_par → H¹ → ⊕_cusps H¹(Γ_c, V) → V_Γ → 0 of Wiese Proposition 4.14.
acceptance: Γ₁(5) (μ = 12, ν∞ = 4): k = 0 gives dim H¹_par = 0 (X₁(5) has genus 0); k = 2 gives dim H¹_par = 2 = 2·dim S₄(Γ₁(5)).
The formula equals 2 dim S_{k+2}(Γ) by the dimension formula (request to ModularForms 10C), the input for Eichler–Shimura.
Γ₁(4), k=1: μ=6, three cusps but two regular, so dim H¹_par=2−2=0. The matrix (1 −1;4 −3) fixes 1/2 and has trace −2; counting all three cusps would give −1.

nodes.title: Petersson detection of period cocycles
nodes.statement: For a torsion-free finite-index Γ≤SL₂(ℤ), the map S_{k+2}(Γ)⊕overline{S_{k+2}(Γ)}→H¹_par(Γ,V_k(ℂ)) given by (f,bar g)↦δ(ψ_f)+overline{δ(ψ_g)} is injective. This is a key input to Eichler–Shimura, independent of the dimension calculation.
hypotheses: k≥0; complex coefficients; the second summand has conjugate scalar multiplication. Coefficient conjugation on cohomology is induced by the real polynomial representation.
proofSteps: Use the determinant pairing on V_k to pair the two coinduced polynomial coefficient modules by summing over Γ\PSL₂(ℤ). Wiese Proposition 6.13 constructs the cusp-relative pairing from a cup-product 2-cocycle and the free-product presentation C₂*C₃; the explicit formula uses only 1/2 and 1/3. Track the row/column coefficient dictionary.

Compute its mixed holomorphic/antiholomorphic value by integrating over the standard fundamental triangle, as in Proposition 6.14, pp.69–70. The unscaled integrals give (2i)^{k+1}μ times the Petersson product. Scaling to ψ=2πi∫ and conjugating the antiholomorphic factor changes it by a nonzero scalar, so vanishing detects the Petersson norm.

The same computation (Stokes' theorem for the closed holomorphic differential) makes the holomorphic/holomorphic and antiholomorphic/antiholomorphic blocks zero. Pair a class in the kernel with the conjugate period class of f to force f=0 by positivity, then with the holomorphic period class of g to force g=0. Base-point coboundaries do not change the pairing on parabolic classes.
acceptance: The sum is checked as a map with two summands; separate injectivity alone is insufficient.
The normalization 2πi is kept in ψ, while Wiese's raw integral has no such factor; only a proved nonzero scalar is used for detection.

sources.locator: §6.3, Propositions 6.13–6.14, pp.66–70; §6.4, proof of Theorem 6.15, pp.70–71
sources.match: Cusp-relative cup pairing, mixed Petersson calculation, and simultaneous detection of the two period summands.

nodes.title: The Eichler–Shimura isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) be of finite index and k ≥ 0. The map S_{k+2}(Γ) ⊕ \overline{S_{k+2}(Γ)} → H¹_par(Γ, V_k(ℂ)), (f, \bar g) ↦ δ(ψ_f) + \overline{δ(ψ_g)}, is an isomorphism compatible with the Hecke and diamond operators; for each sign ±, f ↦ δ((1 ± ι)ψ_f) is an isomorphism S_{k+2}(Γ) ≅ H¹_par(Γ, V_k(ℂ))^± when ι normalises Γ. Via symbols-mod-eisenstein the same holds for Symb_Γ(V_k(ℂ))/Eis_Γ(V_k(ℂ)).
hypotheses: For torsion-free Γ the period/cup-product argument and the general dimension formula apply directly, using c_k. For general Γ descend from the normal torsion-free subgroup Γ∩Γ(M), M≥5, over ℂ. Wiese Theorem 6.15 treats Γ₁(N), N≥4; its odd-weight N=4 dimension input requires the correction E11.
Use the Petersson product and the key period-cocycle injectivity node, and the corrected general finite-index dimension formula imported from ModularForms 10C.

Hecke and diamond compatibility is asserted for the corresponding double cosets and normalizer actions when these are defined for Γ and extend compatibly to the coefficient module. At Γ₁(N) these are the concrete operators planned above.
proofSteps: Well defined and parabolic: δ(ψ_f) is a cocycle whose restriction to every cusp stabiliser is a coboundary (Wiese Propositions 6.7, 6.9).
Injectivity of the combined holomorphic and antiholomorphic map is period-cocycle-injectivity. Injectivity of the two summands individually would not establish injectivity of their sum.
For torsion-free Γ, the corrected dimension is (k+1)μ/6−c_k+2δ_{k,0}=2 dim S_{k+2}(Γ), using ModularForms 10C; injectivity therefore implies bijectivity.

Hecke compatibility: Wiese Proposition 7.24 (the Hecke operators on H¹ match slash operators through the period integrals), and ⟨d⟩ likewise; the ± statements follow as in Wiese Corollary 7.33 by dimension.
Descent to general Γ: apply symbols-level-descent with the Γ/Γ′-action, over ℂ.
acceptance: Γ₀(11), k = 0: H¹_par(Γ₀(11), ℂ) is two-dimensional and S₂(Γ₀(11)) one-dimensional.
Level one, weight 12 (k = 10): H¹_par(SL₂(ℤ), V₁₀(ℂ))^± are one-dimensional, spanned by the images of Δ.
The map on the Eisenstein part: Eis_Γ(V_k(ℂ)) corresponds to Eisenstein series (Wiese Theorem 1.9(a)), not used here.

nodes.title: Modular symbols commute with flat base change
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index, a ring R, a right R[Γ]-module V and a flat R-algebra S, the natural map Symb_Γ(V) ⊗_R S → Symb_Γ(V ⊗_R S) is an isomorphism, compatible with Hecke, diamond and ι actions. In particular Symb_Γ(V_k(K)) ⊗_K ℂ = Symb_Γ(V_k(ℂ)) for a number field K ⊆ ℂ.
hypotheses: Δ₀ is finitely presented over R[Γ] using the finite coset Manin presentation of symbols-coset-description (imported Layer-8 Manin theorem). No finite-presentation hypothesis on V is needed.
proofSteps: Use symbols-coset-description and coset-basis to express Symb_Γ(V) as the kernel of finitely many linear equations V^a→V^b. This works for every finite-index Γ, including groups without T; symbols-generator-values alone has a contains-T restriction.
Kernels commute with flat base change.

Flatness is needed: for p-torsion-free V, Symb_Γ(V) ⊗ 𝔽_p → Symb_Γ(V/p) is injective with cokernel Ext¹_{ℤ[Γ]}(Δ₀, V)[p], which need not vanish (Wiese's faithfulness warning after Proposition 1.8).
Hecke compatibility: T ⊗ 1 corresponds to T.

nodes.title: Newform eigenspaces of modular symbols are one-dimensional
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N)) be a newform of level N with character ε and coefficient field K_f = ℚ(a_n(f), ε). For each sign ±, the subspace Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V_k(K_f))^±[ε][λ_f] on which T_ℓ acts by a_ℓ(f) for every prime ℓ ∤ N is one-dimensional over K_f, it meets Eis_{Γ₁(N)} trivially, and after ⊗ℂ it is spanned by (1 ± ι)ψ_f.
hypotheses: f is a newform at its primitive level N. The pinned finrank_cuspFormsNewEigenspace_eq_one proves dimension one only within the newspace. Use the Layer-4 primitive-associate/oldspace theorem and Layer-5 cross-level uniqueness to rule out lower-conductor old constituents, then apply that pinned theorem.
No Eisenstein eigenform of weight k + 2 and level dividing N has T_ℓ-eigenvalues a_ℓ(f) for all ℓ ∤ N (requested from ModularForms Layer 5).
2 invertible (for ±); K_f contains the values of ε.
proofSteps: The ModularForms 4A/4B old/new decomposition and cross-level uniqueness show that the fixed-character eigenspace with f's eigenvalues at its primitive level N lies entirely in the newspace. The pinned newspace multiplicity-one theorem gives ℂf. Eichler–Shimura and symbols-mod-eisenstein then give a one-dimensional signed quotient eigenspace.

Eis_{Γ₁(N)}(V_k(ℂ)) carries the Hecke eigenvalues of Eisenstein series of weight k + 2 (Wiese Theorem 1.9(a), proved there in Corollary 7.30); by the Layer 5 input none of them is λ_f, so Symb^±[λ_f] ∩ Eis = 0 and Symb^±[λ_f] ≅ (Symb/Eis)^±[λ_f]. To prove surjectivity on eigenspaces, use finite-dimensional spectral separation: a finite linear combination of good Hecke operators separates λ_f from the finitely many boundary characters. Its boundary annihilator is nonzero at λ_f. The resulting polynomial projector lifts every λ_f quotient eigenvector and commutes with the remaining Hecke operators. Vanishing intersection alone would not prove this lifting statement.
Rational structure: Symb(V_k(K_f)) ⊗_{K_f} ℂ = Symb(V_k(ℂ)) (symbols-base-change), and taking λ_f-eigenspaces commutes with this flat base change because λ_f is K_f-valued; so dim_{K_f} = dim_ℂ = 1.
acceptance: For the weight-two newform of level 11, Symb_{Γ₀(11)}(ℚ)^+[λ_f] is spanned by the plus symbol of E = X₀(11).
Level one, Δ: Symb_{SL₂(ℤ)}(V₁₀(ℚ))^±[λ_Δ] is one-dimensional over ℚ.
For an oldform eigensystem the eigenspace is at least two-dimensional; the newform hypothesis is necessary.

nodes.title: Period lines and periods
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N)) be a normalized newform with character ε_N and coefficient field K_f = ℚ(a_n(f), ε_N), with a fixed embedding K_f ↪ ℂ. For each sign ± the period line is L_f^± := Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V_k(K_f))^±[λ_f], a one-dimensional K_f-space (L0/eigenspace-dimension), and ψ_f^± := (1 ± ι)ψ_f lies in L_f^± ⊗_{K_f} ℂ. A period exists only after a basis is chosen: for φ^± ∈ L_f^± ∖ {0}, Ω_f^±(φ^±) ∈ ℂ^× is the scalar with ψ_f^± = Ω_f^±(φ^±)·φ^±. Replacing φ^± by λφ^± (λ ∈ K_f^×) replaces Ω_f^± by λ^{−1}Ω_f^± and every period-normalized value by λ times itself.
hypotheses: ψ_f, ι and the ± decomposition are L0's (period-symbol, involution-at-infinity, plus-minus-decomposition); ι = (−1 0; 0 1) normalizes Γ₁(N).
The line is the object; a scalar period is a coordinate on it. No canonical K_f-basis is assumed (RS-08: 'not a nonexistent canonical integral period basis').
proofSteps: L_f^± ⊗_{K_f} ℂ is the f-isotypic ±-part of Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V_k(ℂ)) by symbols-base-change, and it contains ψ_f^± by the Hecke equivariance of f ↦ ψ_f.
Since the space is one-dimensional and ψ_f^± ≠ 0 (Eichler–Shimura), Ω_f^±(φ^±) exists and is nonzero; Ω(λφ) = λ^{−1}Ω(φ) is immediate.
acceptance: Rescaling a basis by λ multiplies Ω by λ^{−1}: only statements invariant under this are basis-free.
The unsplit f-isotypic eigenspace has dimension two, whereas the span of the single vector ψ_f has dimension one. A scalar period for the whole eigenspace requires two signed coordinates.

nodes.title: Saturated integral lattices and integral periods
nodes.statement: Let 𝒪 be a discrete valuation ring (or a PID) whose fraction field K contains K_f, for example the completion of 𝒪_{K_f} at a prime. Let V_k(𝒪) = 𝒪[X, Y]_k with L0's right action. The saturated lattice L_f^±(𝒪) := (L_f^± ⊗_{K_f} K) ∩ Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V_k(𝒪)) is free of rank one over 𝒪. A generator φ_𝒪^± is unique up to 𝒪^×, so the integral period Ω_{f,𝒪}^± := Ω_f^±(φ_𝒪^±) is canonical up to 𝒪^×. It depends on the lattice V_k(𝒪) (L0/polynomial-duality: V_k(𝒪) and Hom(Sym^k 𝒪², 𝒪) agree only after inverting k!). Comparisons with integral Hecke modules (freeness of the f-part over 𝕋_𝔪, congruence modules) need multiplicity-one hypotheses, which are not assumed here.
hypotheses: Finite generation of Symb_Γ(V_k(𝒪)) comes from Manin's theorem (Div⁰ is finitely generated over ℤ[Γ]; requested from Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 8 by L0).
Multiplicity one enters only when φ_𝒪^± is compared with a generator of a Hecke-module structure; the saturation itself exists for any line.

A local coefficient field has no distinguished complex embedding. Complex scalar periods require an explicitly chosen field embedding into ℂ extending the chosen embedding of K_f; without it, integral periods mean coordinates in the abstract signed line. No continuous ℂ_p-to-ℂ comparison is asserted.
A rank-one eigenline is nonzero. Suggested test declarations explicitly require the chosen vector to be nonzero; the zero span is not a rank-one lattice.
proofSteps: Symb_Γ(V_k(𝒪)) is finitely generated and torsion-free, and embeds in Symb_Γ(V_k(K)) (symbols-base-change, 𝒪 → K flat).
The intersection of a K-line with it is nonzero (clear denominators of a K_f-basis) and finitely generated torsion-free of rank one, hence free over the PID 𝒪.
Saturation: the quotient of Symb_Γ(V_k(𝒪)) by L_f^±(𝒪) is torsion-free by construction, and generators differ by 𝒪^×.
acceptance: k = 0, 𝒪 = ℤ_(p): φ_𝒪^± is the ℤ_(p)-valued symbol in the line whose values are not all divisible by p.

nodes.title: The twisted Mellin formula for modular symbols
nodes.statement: Let f = Σ a_n q^n ∈ S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N)), χ a primitive Dirichlet character of conductor m ≥ 1, τ(χ) = Σ_{a mod m} χ(a)e^{2πia/m}, L(f, χ, s) = Σ χ(n)a_n n^{−s} (entire, in the convention of Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 7), and 0 ≤ j ≤ k. Then, along vertical paths, Σ_{a mod m} χ(a)·2πi∫_{i∞}^{a/m} f(z)(z − a/m)^j dz = τ(χ)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ̄, j+1). Equivalently, with χ̄ for χ, Σ_a χ̄(a)·2πi∫_{i∞}^{a/m} f(z)(z − a/m)^j dz = τ(χ̄)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ, j+1). In symbol form, Σ_a χ(a)·λ_{j,a/m}(ψ_f({a/m} − {∞})) = τ(χ)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ̄, j+1) with λ_{j,x}(P) = (j!/k!)(∂_Y^{k−j}P)(1, −x). For m = 1: 2πi∫_{i∞}^0 f(z)z^j dz = j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, j+1).
hypotheses: The Mellin transform, entire continuation of L(g, s) for cusp forms g, and twisted L-functions are imported from Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 7 (RS-08).

Every convention that changes the formula is explicit. The sum against χ(a) produces L(f, χ̄), not L(f, χ). The Gauss sum is τ(χ) = Σχ(a)e^{2πia/m}. The path runs from i∞ to a/m; reversing it changes the sign. Using −a/m multiplies by χ(−1). The factor 2πi sits in ψ_f, with j!/(−2πi)^j on the right, and not (2πi)^{j+1}.
proofSteps: Birch's lemma: Σ_{a mod m} χ̄(a)e^{2πina/m} = χ(n)τ(χ̄) for primitive χ and every n, so f_χ := Σχ(n)a_n q^n = τ(χ̄)^{−1}Σ_a χ̄(a) f(z + a/m).

Mellin: for a cusp form g, 2πi∫_{i∞}^{0} g(z)z^j dz = −2πi·i^{j+1}∫_0^∞ g(iy)y^j dy = −2πi·i^{j+1}·j!(2π)^{−j−1}L(g, j+1) = j!/(−2πi)^j·L(g, j+1). The integral converges at both ends because g vanishes at every cusp.
Apply this to g = f_χ and substitute w = z + a/m: Σ_a χ̄(a)·2πi∫_{i∞}^{a/m} f(w)(w − a/m)^j dw = τ(χ̄)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ, j+1). Then exchange χ and χ̄.
Symbol form: λ_{j,x}((zX + Y)^k) = (j!/k!)·(k!/j!)(z − x)^j = (z − x)^j.
acceptance: Numerical check with PARI/GP 2.17.2 via cypari2, 2026-09-28, for the characters of order 3 and 6 modulo 7. For 11a1 (k = 0), with the integrals computed through Γ₀(11)-periods, both sides agree to 10^{−14}. For the level-5 weight-4 newform (k = 2) and j = 0, 1, 2, they agree to 10^{−11}. The reading with L(f, χ, j+1) fails by O(1).
For real χ the distinction between χ and χ̄ disappears, so quadratic-twist checks cannot detect a misplaced bar.

nodes.statement: Let T_{j,χ}(ψ) := Σ_{a mod m} χ(a)·λ_{j,a/m}(ψ({a/m} − {∞})) and ε := (−1)^{k−j}χ(−1). Then T_{j,χ}(ψ|ι) = εT_{j,χ}(ψ), so T_{j,χ} vanishes on the −ε eigenspace and T_{j,χ}(ψ_f) = ½T_{j,χ}(ψ_f^ε). For any basis φ^ε of L_f^ε, τ(χ)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ̄, j+1)/Ω_f^ε(φ^ε) = ½T_{j,χ}(φ^ε) ∈ K_f(χ), for 0 ≤ j ≤ k and χ primitive. nodes.title: L-functions of p-stabilized forms
nodes.statement: Let f° be a newform of level N prime to p with character ε_N, α and β the roots of X² − a_pX + ε_N(p)p^{k+1}, and f_α(z) = f°(z) − βf°(pz), so that U_p f_α = αf_α. Then L(f_α, s) = (1 − βp^{−s})L(f°, s), and L(f_α, χ, s) = L(f°, χ, s) for every χ of conductor p^n with n ≥ 1. At s = j+1, βp^{−j−1} = ε_N(p)p^{k−j}/α.

nodes.title: p-stabilisations of a newform
nodes.statement: Let f° = Σ a_n q^n ∈ S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N), ε) be a newform, p ∤ N a prime, and α a root of X² − a_pX + ε(p)p^{k+1}, with β := a_p − α the other root; α ≠ 0 since αβ = ε(p)p^{k+1}. Then f_α(z) := f°(z) − βf°(pz) lies in S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N) ∩ Γ₀(p), ε) ⊆ S_{k+2}(Γ₁(Np)), has coefficients a_n(f_α) = a_n − βa_{n/p} (with a_{n/p} := 0 for p ∤ n), satisfies U_p f_α = αf_α, and T_ℓ f_α = a_ℓ f_α for primes ℓ ∤ Np. On the span of f°(z) and f°(pz), U_p acts by U_p(f°(pz)) = f° and U_p f° = a_p f° − ε(p)p^{k+1}f°(pz), a companion matrix of X² − a_pX + ε(p)p^{k+1}. So each root has a one-dimensional eigenspace in this span, and U_p is semisimple on it if and only if α ≠ β.
hypotheses: The weight is w = k + 2, so the stage's X² − a_pX + ε(p)p^{w−1} is the polynomial here.
The change of Euler factor, L(f_α, s) = (1 − βp^{−s})L(f°, s), is L1/p-stabilised-euler-factors, which takes f_α as defined here.
At p | N there is no stabilisation: the refinement uses the U_p-eigenvalue a_p of the newform itself (refinement).
proofSteps: q-expansion: f°(pz) = V_p f° has coefficients a_{n/p} (Tau Ceti CuspForm.qExpansion_levelRaise), so a_n(f_α) = a_n − βa_{n/p}.

U_p-eigenvalue by coefficients (Tau Ceti heckeUCuspNat_eq_smul_iff_forall_qExpansion_coeff_prime_mul at level Np): a_{pm}(f_α) = a_{pm} − βa_m, while α·a_m(f_α) = αa_m − αβa_{m/p}. These agree because a_{pm} = a_pa_m − ε(p)p^{k+1}a_{m/p} (the good-prime recurrence, heckeTCuspNat_eq_smul_iff_forall_qExpansion_coeff_prime_mul, whose weight k is k + 2 here) and α + β = a_p, αβ = ε(p)p^{k+1}.

The two displayed U_p-relations are the coefficient identities a_{pm}(V_pf°) = a_m(f°) and the same recurrence. A companion matrix is cyclic, so every eigenvalue has geometric multiplicity one, and it is diagonalizable exactly when its two roots differ.
T_ℓ for ℓ ∤ Np commutes with V_p, so f_α has the same good eigenvalues as f°.
acceptance: 11a1 (k = 0) at p = 3: a_3 = −1 and X² + X + 3 has roots of 3-adic valuations 0 and 1; Pollack–Stevens §8 use f_α, f_β of level 33 with f_α|U_3 = αf_α and f_β|U_3 = βf_β.
a_n(f_α) = a_n(f°) for p ∤ n.
f_α ≠ f_β when α ≠ β (their difference is (α − β)f°(pz) ≠ 0), so f° alone does not determine the stabilised form.

nodes.title: Refinements and their slopes
nodes.statement: A refinement at p of a newform f of weight k + 2, level N and character ε is a pair (f, α) with: if p ∤ N, α a root of X² − a_pX + ε(p)p^{k+1}, with refined form f_α (p-stabilisation); if p | N, α = a_p(f) ≠ 0 and refined form f itself. Its slope is h := v_p(α) for a fixed embedding ℚ̄ ↪ ℚ̄_p. The refinement has small slope if h < k + 1 = w − 1, and critical slope if h = k + 1. A refinement is the chosen root together with its eigenline (refined-eigenline); it is not determined by f alone.
hypotheses: Throughout, Γ₀ := Γ₁(N) ∩ Γ₀(p) when p ∤ N and Γ₀ := Γ₁(N) when p | N. Pollack–Stevens work with Γ₀ = Γ ∩ Γ₀(p) for Γ of level prime to p. Their proofs use only that Γ₀ ⊆ Σ₀(p) has finite index (for Corollary 2.10, here L0/symbols-generator-values) and that U_p = Σ_{a=0}^{p−1}|β(a, p) with β(a, p) = (1 a; 0 p). Both hold for Γ₁(N) with p | N (L0/hecke-operators-gamma1), which is the stage's case of p dividing the level.
α is an algebraic integer, so h ≥ 0. When p ∤ N, αβ = ε(p)p^{k+1} with β integral gives v_p(α) + v_p(β) = k + 1, so 0 ≤ h ≤ k + 1.

When p | N and a_p ≠ 0, the slope is k/2 in the case p ‖ N with ε of conductor prime to p (a_p² = ε(p)p^k, the bad-prime eigenvalue milestone of Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 4). This is used only in examples.
proofSteps: Well-definedness is immediate; the slope bound is the valuation identity above.
acceptance: p-ordinary f (a_p a p-adic unit, p ∤ N): one refinement of slope 0 and one of slope k + 1, which is critical.
11a1 at p = 3: slopes 0 and 1 (Pollack–Stevens §8).
p | N with a_p = 0 (for example p² | N with ε of conductor prime to p): no refinement.

nodes.title: The refined eigenline
nodes.statement: Let (f, α) be a refinement, K ⊇ K_f(α) a field, and λ the system of eigenvalues a_ℓ (ℓ ∤ Np) and α (for U_p). For each sign ±, L_{f,α}^± := Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k(K))^±[ε][λ] is one-dimensional over K; after ⊗ℂ it is spanned by (1 ± ι)ψ_{f_α} (with f_α := f when p | N). For p ∤ N it lies in the two-dimensional subspace where only the T_ℓ (ℓ ∤ Np) act by a_ℓ, on which U_p acts by the companion matrix of X² − a_pX + ε(p)p^{k+1}. For p | N, L_{f,α}^± is L1's line L_f^±, on which U_p acts by a_p.
hypotheses: Throughout, Γ₀ := Γ₁(N) ∩ Γ₀(p) when p ∤ N and Γ₀ := Γ₁(N) when p | N. Pollack–Stevens work with Γ₀ = Γ ∩ Γ₀(p) for Γ of level prime to p. Their proofs use only that Γ₀ ⊆ Σ₀(p) has finite index (for Corollary 2.10, here L0/symbols-generator-values) and that U_p = Σ_{a=0}^{p−1}|β(a, p) with β(a, p) = (1 a; 0 p). Both hold for Γ₁(N) with p | N (L0/hecke-operators-gamma1), which is the stage's case of p dividing the level.

Forms-level input, requested from Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 4: for p ∤ N, the subspace of S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N) ∩ Γ₀(p), ε) on which T_ℓ acts by a_ℓ(f) for all ℓ ∤ Np is spanned by f(z) and f(pz); for p | N, U_p f = a_p f.

Eisenstein separation at level Np: no Eisenstein eigensystem of weight k + 2 and level dividing Np equals (a_ℓ(f))_{ℓ ∤ Np} (requested from Layer 5; L0/eigenspace-dimension requests the level-N form).
proofSteps: Over ℂ: by L0/eichler-shimura-isomorphism for Γ₀, L0/symbols-mod-eisenstein and the Eisenstein separation, the subspace of Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k(ℂ))^±[ε] where T_ℓ acts by a_ℓ (ℓ ∤ Np) is isomorphic, Hecke-equivariantly including U_p (L0/period-symbol: ψ_{U_p g} = ψ_g|U_p), to the corresponding subspace span(f(z), f(pz)) of S_{k+2}(Γ₀, ε). Use the same boundary spectral projector as eigenspace-dimension at level Np, commuting with U_p as well as the good Hecke operators; no semisimplicity of the full symbol space is assumed.
By p-stabilisation, U_p acts on span(f(z), f(pz)) by a cyclic companion matrix, so the α-eigenspace is ℂf_α, and its image under the ±-part of Eichler–Shimura is ℂ(1 ± ι)ψ_{f_α}.
Rationality: λ is K-valued and Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k(K)) ⊗_K ℂ = Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k(ℂ)) (L0/symbols-base-change), so dim_K = dim_ℂ = 1.
p | N: L1/period-lines gives the line; U_p commutes with the T_ℓ, so it preserves the line, and it acts there by a_p because U_p f = a_p f and ψ is U_p-equivariant.
acceptance: 11a1 at p = 3: Pollack–Stevens use the symbols φ^±_β at level 33 attached to f_β (§8).
For p ∤ N the subspace cut out by the T_ℓ (ℓ ∤ Np) alone is two-dimensional: dropping U_p loses the line.
If α = β the U_p-eigenspace is still a line, but the generalized eigenspace is two-dimensional, and slope decompositions see the generalized eigenspace.

nodes.title: Distribution modules with the weight-k action
nodes.statement: For r ∈ |ℂ_p^×|, let A[r] be the ℚ_p-Banach algebra of affinoid functions on B[ℤ_p, r] (the points within r of ℤ_p), A(ℤ_p) = lim_{s>0} A[s] and A†(ℤ_p, r) = lim_{s>r} A[s], with continuous duals D(ℤ_p), D[r] and D†(ℤ_p, r); write D = D[1] and D† = D†(ℤ_p, 1). For r < p, Σ₀(p) := {(a b; c d) ∈ M₂(ℤ_p) : p ∤ a, p | c, ad − bc ≠ 0} acts on A[r] by (γ ·_k f)(z) = (a + cz)^k f((b + dz)/(a + cz)), and on distributions on the right by (μ|_kγ)(f) = μ(γ ·_k f). The resulting modules are D_k(ℤ_p), D_k and D†_k. Moments: μ ↦ (μ(z^j))_j identifies D† with the sequences that are O(r^j) for every r > 1, and D, as a Banach space, with the bounded sequences. For r < p, γ ∈ Σ₀(p) with det γ = p^n and μ ∈ D[r], ‖μ|γ‖_{r/p^n} ≤ ‖μ‖_r.
hypotheses: The spaces A[r], D[r], D(ℤ_p) and their topologies are requested from LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0; the weight-k action and the moment description are built here.
The restriction r < p is needed: for r ≥ p the formula does not preserve A[r] (sourceIssues E8). Every space the stage uses has r ≤ 1 or r slightly above 1.
proofSteps: Proposition 3.1: |μ(z^j)| ≤ ‖z^j‖_r‖μ‖_r = r^j‖μ‖_r gives the growth; conversely, a sequence of that growth defines μ(Σ a_jz^j) := Σ a_jc_j on A†(ℤ_p, 1), since f ∈ A[r] for some r > 1. On D, ‖μ‖_1 = sup_j |μ(z^j)|.

Action and contraction: for r < p and z ∈ B[ℤ_p, r], |cz| < 1 when |z| ≤ max(1, r), so a + cz is a unit and (a + cz)^k has absolute value 1. For z₀ ∈ ℤ_p and |w| ≤ r, |γ(z₀ + w) − γz₀| = |det γ|·|w|/|(a + cz₀)(a + c(z₀ + w))| = p^{−n}|w|, and γz₀ ∈ ℤ_p. So γ maps B[ℤ_p, r] into B[ℤ_p, r/p^n], f ↦ γ ·_k f maps A[r/p^n] into A[r] with norm at most 1, and dualising gives the bound used in the proof of Lemma 6.2.
acceptance: The Dirac distribution δ₀ has moments (1, 0, 0, …) and lies in D.
c_j = 1/(j + 1) is O(r^j) for every r > 1 but unbounded (|1/p^m|_p = p^m), so it defines an element of D† not in D; such denominators are why Theorem 4.5 needs D† (Remark 4.6).
c_j = p^{−j} is not O(r^j) for 1 < r < p, so it is the moment sequence of no element of D†.

nodes.statement: For D_k one of D_k(ℤ_p), D_k, D†_k, the map ρ_k : D_k → V_k(ℚ_p), μ ↦ ∫(Y − zX)^k dμ(z) (coefficientwise), is Σ₀(p)-equivariant for the weight-k action and L0's right action (P|γ)(X, Y) = P(dX − cY, −bX + aY). nodes.statement: ρ*_k : Symb_{Γ₀}(D†_k) → Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k) is surjective, by an explicit lift of the values on the generators. For μ ∈ D†_k, μ|β(a, p) ∈ D_k, so U_p maps Symb_{Γ₀}(D†_k) into Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k). Consequently every classical symbol in a generalized U_p-eigenspace with nonzero eigenvalue has a D_k-valued lift. This is surjectivity onto that finite-slope target, not a global surjectivity assertion for D_k.
hypotheses: Throughout, Γ₀ := Γ₁(N) ∩ Γ₀(p) when p ∤ N and Γ₀ := Γ₁(N) when p | N. Pollack–Stevens work with Γ₀ = Γ ∩ Γ₀(p) for Γ of level prime to p. Their proofs use only that Γ₀ ⊆ Σ₀(p) has finite index (for Corollary 2.10, here L0/symbols-generator-values) and that U_p = Σ_{a=0}^{p−1}|β(a, p) with β(a, p) = (1 a; 0 p). Both hold for Γ₁(N) with p | N (L0/hecke-operators-gamma1), which is the stage's case of p dividing the level.

The generator-and-relation description is L0/symbols-generator-values, with the D_∞ relation of sourceIssues E1. Pollack–Stevens' proof of Theorem 5.1 uses the printed relation (µ∞|Δ = ν∞); it works verbatim with ν∞ replaced by −ν∞.
The bounded-valued lift conclusion assumes a nonzero U_p eigenvalue (Corollary 5.4); no claim is made on the zero-eigenvalue part.
proofSteps: Difference equation (Theorem 4.5): for ν ∈ D†_k of total measure zero, μ := Σ_{j≥1} ν(z^j)/j · η_{j−1}, with η_j(z^r) = C(r, j)b_{r−j} (Bernoulli numbers, Lemma 4.4), is the unique solution of μ|Δ = ν, Δ = (1 1; 0 1) − 1. By von Staudt–Clausen and Proposition 3.1 it lies in D†_k. Uniqueness is Lemma 4.3.

Theorem 5.1: lift φ(D_i) arbitrarily, lift φ(D′_i) and φ(D″_i) through the idempotents of Proposition 4.1 (2 and 3 are invertible on the ℚ_p-space D†_k), and solve for the value at D_∞ with the difference equation. Its right side has total measure zero because the Y^k-coefficient of every element of Δ(V_k) vanishes (Proposition 4.2). The resulting value can miss φ(D_∞) by cX^k (ker Δ on V_k is ℚ_pX^k); adjusting the lifts of the φ(D_i) corrects the k-th moment.
Lemma 5.3: (μ|β(a, p))(z^j) = Σ_r C(j, r)a^{j−r}p^rμ(z^r), and (p^rμ(z^r))_r is bounded by Proposition 3.1.
Corollary 5.4: it suffices to lift φ in a generalized U_p-eigenspace with eigenvalue λ ≠ 0. Write φ = φ′|U_p, lift φ′ to Ψ′ over D†_k, and take Ψ′|U_p.
acceptance: k = 0, Γ₀(11) (Pollack's §2.6 generators): the lift is explicit on three divisors.
Without the correction step the D_∞-value can be off by cX^k; Remark 5.2 notes that for a non-Eisenstein eigensymbol, applying T_ℓ − (ℓ^{k+1} + 1) removes the error instead.
Theorem 4.5 fails in D_k: the solution can have unbounded moments (Remark 4.6).

nodes.title: Slope decomposition of the fibre of specialisation
nodes.statement: Let ϕ ∈ Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k) ⊗ K be a Hecke eigensymbol, K/ℚ_p finite, with U_p-eigenvalue λ of slope h with 0≤h≤k+1, and X_ϕ := (ρ*_k)^{−1}(K·ϕ) ⊆ Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k) ⊗ K. Then X_ϕ = X_ϕ^{(=h)} ⊕ X_ϕ^{(>h)} uniquely, with u := λ^{−1}U_p topologically nilpotent on X_ϕ^{(>h)}, invertible on X_ϕ^{(=h)} with (u^{−n}) bounded, X_ϕ^{(=h)} finite-dimensional over K, and projection x ↦ lim_n u^{n!}x.
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p is finite and 0≤h=v_p(λ)≤k+1. Import the field/lattice ordinary–nilpotent decomposition from LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4, in the precise requested form of Pollack–Stevens Lemma 5.5 and Proposition 5.6. The supplier’s affinoid finite-slope theorem assumes (Pr); that hypothesis is not silently imposed or inferred here.

Complete continuity of U_p on Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k): each |β(a, p) maps D[1] into D[1/p] (weight-k-distributions), and the natural map D[1/p] → D[1] is dual to the completely continuous restriction A[1] → A[1/p] (Pollack–Stevens §3.1).
proofSteps: Lattice: Y_ϕ := {Φ in the unit ball of X_ϕ : |Φ(D)(z^j)| ≤ p^{−(h−j)} for 0 ≤ j ≤ ⌊h⌋ and all D ∈ Δ₀}.

u preserves Y_ϕ: (Φ|u)(D)(z^r) = λ^{−1}Σ_a Σ_j C(r, j)a^{r−j}p^jΦ(D_a)(z^j) with D_a = β(a, p)D, and each |p^jΦ(D_a)(z^j)| ≤ p^{−h} (by the defining bound for j ≤ ⌊h⌋ and because j > h otherwise), so |(Φ|u)(D)(z^r)| ≤ 1. Membership in Y_ϕ depends only on ρ*_k(Φ), and ρ*_k(Φ|u) = ρ*_k(Φ). At h=k+1 the j=k+1 bound is exactly the unit-ball bound and imposes no extra condition; the other bounds involve only the moments detected by ρ_k. This is where the slope upper bound is used.
The unit ball itself need not be u-stable (Pollack–Stevens' footnote (3)), which is why Y_ϕ is used.

Y_φ is closed, bounded and spans X_φ: it is given by closed moment inequalities, and multiplying any vector by a sufficiently small scalar satisfies them. Finite Manin generators put the symbol Banach space inside a finite product of distribution Banach spaces. Complete continuity gives finite image on Y_φ/π^nY_φ; apply Lemma 5.5 at each quotient, pass to the complete inverse limit, and tensor with K. This is the field/lattice decomposition requested from the existing operator-theory owner (Proposition 5.6). No affinoid (Pr) assertion is used.
acceptance: h = 0: Y_ϕ is the whole unit ball, and the projector is Hida's ordinary projector lim U_p^{n!} up to the unit λ.
X_ϕ is infinite-dimensional (it contains ker ρ*_k), while X_ϕ^{(=h)} is finite-dimensional.
For h > 0 the unit ball of X_ϕ need not be preserved by u.

nodes.title: Stevens' control theorem in small slope
nodes.statement: Specialisation induces isomorphisms Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k(ℤ_p))^{(<k+1)} ≅ Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k)^{(<k+1)} ≅ Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k)^{(<k+1)} of the subspaces on which U_p acts with slope < k + 1, compatible with the Hecke operators and ι. In particular, for a refinement (f, α) of slope h < k + 1 and each basis φ^± of the refined eigenline, there is a unique Φ^± ∈ Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k(ℤ_p))^± with ρ*_k(Φ^±) = φ^±, and Φ^± is a Hecke eigensymbol with the eigenvalues of f_α.
hypotheses: Throughout, Γ₀ := Γ₁(N) ∩ Γ₀(p) when p ∤ N and Γ₀ := Γ₁(N) when p | N. Pollack–Stevens work with Γ₀ = Γ ∩ Γ₀(p) for Γ of level prime to p. Their proofs use only that Γ₀ ⊆ Σ₀(p) has finite index (for Corollary 2.10, here L0/symbols-generator-values) and that U_p = Σ_{a=0}^{p−1}|β(a, p) with β(a, p) = (1 a; 0 p). Both hold for Γ₁(N) with p | N (L0/hecke-operators-gamma1), which is the stage's case of p dividing the level.

Pollack–Stevens cite the first isomorphism (independence of the radius on the finite-slope part) to their critical-slope preprint [16, Lemma 5.2], which was not read. Here it is derived from the contraction of weight-k-distributions. For Φ in the finite-slope part of Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k) (finite-dimensional by the Riesz theory), Φ = (Φ|U_p^{−n})|U_p^n with Φ|U_p^{−n} in the same space, and |U_p^n = Σ_{a mod p^n}|β(a, p^n) maps D[1]-valued symbols to D[1/p^n]-valued ones. So Φ takes values in every D[1/p^n], hence in D(ℤ_p) = lim_s D[s] (the maps D[s] → D[1] are injective).
proofSteps: Injectivity on slope < k + 1: for Φ ∈ ker ρ*_k, (Φ|U_p)(D)(z^r) = Σ_a Σ_j C(r, j)a^{r−j}p^jΦ(D_a)(z^j), and the terms with j ≤ k vanish, so U_p is divisible by p^{k+1} on ker ρ*_k: its slopes there are ≥ k + 1.

Surjectivity (Theorem 5.9 with Lemma 5.10): for an eigensymbol ϕ of slope h, ρ*_k maps X_ϕ^{(=h)} onto K·ϕ (overconvergent-lift, slope-decomposition-fibre; ρ*_k kills X_ϕ^{(>h)}). When h < k + 1 this map is also injective, so the eigensymbol it produces lifts a nonzero multiple of ϕ.
An isomorphism after extending scalars to ℚ̄_p is one before.
Uniqueness of Φ^± and its eigen-property follow from the Hecke-equivariant isomorphism and the one-dimensionality of the refined eigenline.
acceptance: h = 0: Hida's ordinary control theorem for Γ₀.

At h = k + 1 specialisation can fail to be an isomorphism on the f-part: by Theorem 5.14 it fails exactly for f in the image of θ_k, which includes the critical-slope stabilisation of a p-ordinary CM form (Remark 5.15). That is stage L3.
The threshold is strict: slope k + 1 = w − 1 is excluded.

nodes.title: Values of slope-h eigensymbols are h-admissible
nodes.statement: If Φ ∈ Symb_{Γ₀}(D(ℤ_p)) is a U_p-eigensymbol whose eigenvalue λ has slope h, then every value Φ(D) is h-admissible: ‖Φ(D)‖_r = O(r^{−h}) as r → 0⁺.
hypotheses: h-admissibility (Pollack–Stevens Definition 6.1) and its theory are requested from LocallyAnalyticDistributions L2.
proofSteps: For 0 < r ≤ 1, n ≥ 1 and D ∈ Δ₀: ‖Φ(D)‖_{r/p^n} = |λ|^{−n}‖(Φ|U_p^n)(D)‖_{r/p^n} ≤ |λ|^{−n} max_a ‖Φ(β(a, p^n)D)|β(a, p^n)‖_{r/p^n} ≤ |λ|^{−n} max_a ‖Φ(β(a, p^n)D)‖_r ≤ |λ|^{−n}‖Φ‖_r, by the contraction of weight-k-distributions.
|λ|^{−n} = p^{nh} = (r/(r/p^n))^h, so ‖Φ(D)‖_s ≤ (r^h‖Φ‖_r)·s^{−h} for s = r/p^n, which is O(s^{−h}).
acceptance: h = 0: the values are bounded, that is, measures.
λ = 0 is not covered (infinite slope).
At h = k + 1, h-admissibility no longer determines a distribution from its values on locally polynomial functions of degree ≤ k (Pollack–Stevens §6.4; stage L3).

nodes.title: The p-adic L-function of a small-slope refinement
nodes.statement: Let (f, α) be a refinement of slope h < k + 1, φ^± bases of the refined eigenlines, Φ^± their eigenlifts (control-theorem) and Φ := Φ⁺ + Φ⁻. Define L_p(f, α; φ^±) := Φ({∞} − {0})|_{ℤ_p^×} ∈ D(ℤ_p^×). It is h-admissible, and for every locally analytic g, Φ({∞} − {0})(g·1_{a+p^nℤ_p}) = α^{−n}Φ({∞} − {a/p^n})(g(a + p^nz)) (the distribution relation). Write the bases as Pollack–Stevens do, φ^±({r} − {s}) = (∫_r^s f_α(z)(zX + Y)^k dz ± (−1)^k∫_{−r}^{−s} f_α(z)(zX − Y)^k dz)·πi/Ω^±, which defines Ω^± ∈ ℂ^× from φ^±. Then for p ∤ a and 0 ≤ j ≤ k the ±-part of L_p(z^j·1_{a+p^nℤ_p}) is α^{−n}(∫_∞^{a/p^n}(−p^nz + a)^j f_α(z)dz ± ∫_∞^{−a/p^n}(p^nz + a)^j f_α(z)dz)·πi/Ω^±, which is Pollack–Stevens (2).
hypotheses: The construction depends on the refinement α and on the bases φ^±; rescaling φ^± by c^± ∈ K^× rescales the ±-parts of L_p by c^±.

In L0's normalization ψ_f({s} − {r}) = 2πi∫_r^s f(z)(zX + Y)^k dz, with ι acting on V_k by P(X, Y) ↦ P(X, −Y), the displayed φ^± is −(1 ± (−1)^kι)ψ_{f_α}/(2Ω^±). So Pollack–Stevens' label ± is the ι-sign times (−1)^k, and Ω^± = −½Ω_{f_α}^{±(−1)^k}(φ^±) in the notation of L1/period-lines.
Orientation: the divisor is {∞} − {0}; the choice {0} − {∞} changes L_p by −1.
proofSteps: Distribution relation (proof of Proposition 6.3): Φ({∞} − {0}) = α^{−n}(Φ|U_p^n)({∞} − {0}) = α^{−n}Σ_{a mod p^n}Φ({∞} − {a/p^n})|β(a, p^n), and μ|β(a, p^n) is supported on a + p^nℤ_p, where (μ|β(a, p^n))(g) = μ(g(a + p^nz)).
For deg Q ≤ k, Φ^±({∞} − {a/p^n})(Q) is read off from ρ*_k(Φ^±) = φ^± through ρ_k; with Q(z) = (p^nz + a)^j this gives (2).
h-admissibility is eigensymbol-admissibility applied to D = {∞} − {0}.
The relation with ψ: the first integral is ψ_{f_α}({s} − {r})/(2Ω^±) = −ψ_{f_α}({r} − {s})/(2Ω^±), and (ψ|ι)({r} − {s}) = ψ({−r} − {−s})|ι = −2πi∫_{−r}^{−s} f_α(z)(zX − Y)^k dz.
acceptance: k = 0: L_p(1_{a+p^nℤ_p}) = α^{−n}φ({∞} − {a/p^n}) for p ∤ a, the Riemann sums of the modular symbol of f_α.
Replacing φ^+ by 2φ^+ doubles the +-part only.
The divisor {0} − {∞} gives −L_p: the orientation is part of the definition.

nodes.title: Interpolation and uniqueness of the p-adic L-function
nodes.statement: Let (f, α) have slope h < k + 1, with φ^± and Ω^± as in p-adic-l-function, 0 ≤ j ≤ k, and χ a character of ℤ_p^× of conductor p^n. With ± := (−1)^jχ(−1), L_p(f, α; φ^±)(z^j·χ) = e·α^{−n}p^{nj}·τ(χ)·j!/(2πi)^j·L(f_α, χ^{−1}, j + 1)/Ω^±, where e = 1 if n ≥ 1 and e = 1 − p^j/α if n = 0 (χ trivial). For p ∤ N and n = 0, L(f_α, j + 1) = (1 − ε(p)p^{k−j}/α)L(f, j + 1) supplies the second Euler factor. In L1's notation I_j(x) = 2πi∫_{i∞}^x f_α(z)(z − x)^j dz, the right side for n ≥ 1 is ±α^{−n}p^{nj}Σ_{a mod p^n}χ(a)I_j(−a/p^n)/Ω^±. This is RJW Theorem B.1 with Ω_{B.1}^± = −Ω^±/(2πi), a j-independent conversion. Moreover, L_p(f, α; φ^±) is the unique h-admissible distribution on ℤ_p^× with these values, because h < k + 1.
hypotheses: Pollack–Stevens (1) prints the formula as α^{−n}p^{n(j+1)}/(−2πi)^j·j!/τ(χ^{−1})·L(f, χ^{−1}, j+1)/Ω^±. It agrees with (2), and hence with Proposition 6.3, only up to the sign ± (sourceIssues E4), and it omits e at n = 0 (sourceIssues E5). The statement here is the one (2) implies.

Uniqueness of an h-admissible distribution from its values on locally polynomial functions of degree ≤ k when h < k + 1 (Amice–Vélu, Višik) is requested from LocallyAnalyticDistributions L2. At h = k + 1 it fails (stage L3).
proofSteps: Case n ≥ 1: sum (2) against χ(a) over a mod p^n with p ∤ a. With (−p^nz + a)^j = (−p^n)^j(z − a/p^n)^j and (p^nz + a)^j = p^{nj}(z + a/p^n)^j, the ±-part is α^{−n}p^{nj}[(−1)^jS ± Σ_aχ(a)I_j(−a/p^n)]/(2Ω^±), where S := Σ_aχ(a)I_j(a/p^n). Substituting a ↦ −a gives Σ_aχ(a)I_j(−a/p^n) = χ(−1)S, so the ±-part vanishes unless ± = (−1)^jχ(−1), and then equals α^{−n}p^{nj}(−1)^jS/Ω^±.
L1/twisted-mellin-formula: S = τ(χ)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f_α, χ̄, j + 1), which gives the formula with e = 1.

Case n = 0: L_p(z^j) = Φ({∞} − {0})(z^j) − Φ({∞} − {0})(z^j·1_{pℤ_p}), and by the distribution relation with a = 0, n = 1 the second term is α^{−1}p^jΦ({∞} − {0})(z^j). So L_p(z^j) = (1 − p^j/α)·Φ({∞} − {0})(z^j), and the case a = 0, n = 0 of the computation above evaluates Φ({∞} − {0})(z^j). L1/p-stabilised-euler-factors converts L(f_α, j + 1).

RJW comparison: L1/rjw-b1-comparison writes B.1's right side as −ε(−1)^k/(2πi·Ω_{B.1})·α^{−n}p^{nj}Σ_aχ(a)I_j(−a/p^n) with ε = (−1)^{k−j}χ(−1), so ε(−1)^k = (−1)^jχ(−1) = ±. Comparing with the formula above gives Ω_{B.1}^± = −Ω^±/(2πi).

Uniqueness: two h-admissible distributions with h < k + 1 that agree on locally polynomial functions of degree ≤ k are equal (LAD L2). The values on z^j·1_{a+p^nℤ_p}, given by (2), determine L_p on such functions.
acceptance: k = 0, n = 0, p ∤ N, trivial ε: L_p(1) = (1 − 1/α)²·L(f, 1)/Ω^+, the Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum shape.
For quadratic χ, and on the +-part, (1) as printed and (2) agree; only the −-part carries the sign of E4.
Replacing L(f_α, χ^{−1}, j + 1) by L(f_α, χ, j + 1) is wrong for non-real χ (L1's numerical check of the twisted Mellin formula).

nodes.title: Ordinary p-adic L-functions as integral measures
nodes.statement: Let (f, α) have slope 0, 𝒪 the integers of a finite extension K of ℚ_p containing K_f(α), and φ^± generators of the saturated lattices L_{f,α}^±(𝒪) := L_{f,α}^± ∩ Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k(𝒪)). Then L_p(f, α; φ^±) is a measure with values in 𝒪: for p ∤ a, L_p(1_{a+p^nℤ_p}) = α^{−n}·[Y^k](φ({∞} − {a/p^n})) ∈ 𝒪, where φ := φ⁺ + φ⁻ and [Y^k] is the Y^k-coefficient. So L_p ∈ 𝒪⟦ℤ_p^×⟧. Boundedness alone, that is h = 0 with arbitrary bases φ^±, gives only an element of 𝒪⟦ℤ_p^×⟧[1/p].
hypotheses: The saturated lattice of a line and its generator, unique up to 𝒪^×, are L1/integral-period-lattices. Its proof uses only that the line lies in Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k(K)) for a finite-index Γ₀, so it applies to the refined eigenline.
The identification of 0-admissible distributions with bounded measures, K ⊗ 𝒪⟦ℤ_p^×⟧, is requested from LocallyAnalyticDistributions L2 (order zero).
proofSteps: Distribution relation with g = 1: L_p(1_{a+p^nℤ_p}) = α^{−n}Φ({∞} − {a/p^n})(1), and Φ(D)(1) is the Y^k-coefficient of ρ_k(Φ(D)) = φ(D) (specialisation-map), with no binomial denominator.

α ∈ 𝒪^× and φ(D) ∈ V_k(𝒪), so every value on a compact open is in 𝒪. By eigensymbol-admissibility L_p is 0-admissible, hence a bounded measure, and it is determined by its values on compact opens, so it lies in 𝒪⟦ℤ_p^×⟧.
For bases p^{−m}·(integral generator) the values lie in p^{−m}𝒪.
Approximate any continuous O-valued function by locally constant O-valued functions; completeness and the compact-open bound imply integral limits. Thus all polynomial moments are integral.
acceptance: 11a1 at p = 3 with the unit root α ∈ ℤ_3^× of X² + X + 3 (≡ −1 mod 3 by Hensel): L_p ∈ ℤ_3⟦ℤ_3^×⟧ for the integral generators φ^±.
p^{−1}φ^± in place of φ^± gives a bounded measure in p^{−1}𝒪⟦ℤ_p^×⟧, in general not in 𝒪⟦ℤ_p^×⟧.

Once the compact-open values define an O-valued measure, integrating any continuous O-valued function is O-valued. In particular all moments μ(z^j) are integral, even for p≤k. The polynomial lattice alone does not prove this via division by C(k,j); the ordinary eigenrelation and measure integrality supply the extra divisibility.

nodes.title: The critical-slope p-adic L-function of a non-θ-critical refinement
nodes.statement: Let (f, α) be a refinement of critical slope h = k + 1 (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L2 refinement) that is not θ-critical (equivalently non-critical, by PadicFamilies L3). Then each refined eigenline φ^± has a unique overconvergent eigen-lift Φ^± ∈ Symb_Γ(D_k)^± with ρ*_k(Φ^±) = φ^±, and L_p(f, α; φ^±) := Φ({∞} − {0})|_{ℤ_p^×} with Φ = Φ⁺ + Φ⁻. It is (k + 1)-admissible, satisfies the distribution relation of L2, and its PS-labelled ±-parts (L0 signs (−1)^k times those labels) are Bellaïche's L±(f_α, ·) with the scalars fixed by ρ*_k(Φ^±) = φ^± (so the periods Ω^± are those of L2).
hypotheses: Critical slope and not θ-critical; the uniqueness of the lift is Pollack–Stevens' Theorem 5.14 / Bellaïche's Theorem 1 with e = 1 (PadicFamilies L3).

For the Bellaïche/PadicFamilies import, f is a cuspidal newform of tame level N with p∤N; the two Hecke roots are distinct. Bellaïche's involution is diag(1,−1), whereas L0 uses diag(−1,1): Bellaïche/PS sign s corresponds to L0 sign (−1)^k s. Apply this sign dictionary before identifying signed eigenlines.

Non-θ-critical cuspidal refinements are non-critical and hence decent by Bellaïche Definition 1(ii). The specialization certificate in the suggested file is the explicit supplier obligation, not a proof of this hypothesis.
proofSteps: By PadicFamilies L3 (e = 1), ρ*_k restricts to an isomorphism of the f_α-eigenspaces, so the lifts exist and are unique; evaluate at {∞} − {0} as in L2.
Admissibility of order k + 1: the U_p-eigenvalue has valuation k + 1 (Višik's criterion).
acceptance: The normalisation is by specialisation, not by values: at critical slope values do not determine the distribution.

nodes.statement: For (f, α) as in non-theta-critical-lift, 0 ≤ j ≤ k and χ of conductor p^n, L_p(f, α; φ^±)(z^j·χ) is given by the formula of L2's interpolation-and-uniqueness (with ± = (−1)^jχ(−1), the factor α^{−n}p^{nj}τ(χ)j!/(2πi)^j, the Euler factor 1 − p^j/α when n = 0, and L(f_α, χ^{−1}, j + 1)/Ω^±).
hypotheses: The formula is a formal consequence of Φ being a U_p-eigensymbol lifting φ⁺ + φ⁻; Pollack–Stevens (3) prints the L-value at 1 (recorded as E6).
proofSteps: Evaluate Φ({∞} − {0}) on z^j·1_{a+p^nℤ_p} with the distribution relation and ρ*_k(Φ) = φ⁺ + φ⁻, then use the twisted Mellin formula of L1, exactly as in L2.

nodes.title: Interpolation does not determine critical-slope L-functions
nodes.statement: At h = k + 1 there are nonzero (k + 1)-admissible distributions on ℤ_p^× vanishing at every z^j·χ (0 ≤ j ≤ k, χ of finite order): for each tame character ψ, the distribution whose Mellin transform in the variable s is log^{[k]}(s) = ∏_{i=0}^{k} log_p(γ^{−i}s). Hence the interpolation values do not determine L_p(f, α; φ^±); its uniqueness is the uniqueness of the eigen-lift, not of an admissible distribution.
hypotheses: Amice–Vélu–Višik uniqueness holds only for h < k + 1 (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L2).

At odd p use torsion part μ_{p−1} and γ generating 1+pZ_p; at p=2 use μ₂={±1} and γ generating 1+4Z₂. The logarithmic product is constructed on a fixed torsion component; it vanishes at every classical finite-order character on that component.
proofSteps: log^{[k]} has order exactly k + 1 and vanishes at s = γ^jζ for all p-power roots of unity ζ and 0 ≤ j ≤ k, which are exactly the images of the characters z^jχ.
Adding a multiple of it to L_p preserves all interpolation values and (k + 1)-admissibility.
acceptance: Do not extend the strict inequality h < k + 1 of the uniqueness theorem by continuity.

nodes.title: θ-critical single forms
nodes.statement: For a decent θ-critical cuspidal refinement at a prime not dividing the tame level (for example the critical-slope refinement of a CM form with p split, such as X₀(32) at p = 5), L2's construction does not apply: the eigenline of Symb_Γ(D_k)^± lies in ker ρ*_k (PadicFamilies L3, Bellaïche's theorem), Bellaïche's L± vanishes at all classical characters, and the classical interpolation is carried by the top secondary L-function L±_{e−1}, normalised by ρ*_k of the top generalised eigenvector = φ^±.
hypotheses: e = dim Symb^±_Γ(D_k)(f_β) ≥ 2 at a θ-critical cuspidal point.

For the Bellaïche/PadicFamilies import, f is a cuspidal newform of tame level N with p∤N; the two Hecke roots are distinct. Bellaïche's involution is diag(1,−1), whereas L0 uses diag(−1,1): Bellaïche/PS sign s corresponds to L0 sign (−1)^k s. Apply this sign dictionary before identifying signed eigenlines.
The refinement is decent; then e≥2 follows for a θ-critical cuspidal point. CM forms satisfy decency by Proposition 2.15(iv). No theorem for an arbitrary non-decent point is asserted.
proofSteps: Theorem 1 of Bellaïche gives the eigenline in ker ρ*_k; Theorem 2 the vanishing; §1.4.5 the interpolation of L_{e−1}.

nodes.title: Comparing critical and arithmetic L-functions through families
nodes.statement: Let V ∋ x be the affinoid neighbourhood of a decent critical-slope point in the eigencurve with two-variable L±(y, σ) (PadicFamilies L3). If an identity between L±(y, ·) and an arithmetic construction (e.g. Kato's) holds, up to the normalising function of y, at a Zariski-dense set of non-critical classical points y ∈ V, it holds at x; comparisons at x by interpolation values alone are not valid.
hypotheses: Both sides analytic in y on V; the normalising function of y is nonvanishing.

For the Bellaïche/PadicFamilies import, f is a cuspidal newform of tame level N with p∤N; the two Hecke roots are distinct. Bellaïche's involution is diag(1,−1), whereas L0 uses diag(−1,1): Bellaïche/PS sign s corresponds to L0 sign (−1)^k s. Apply this sign dictionary before identifying signed eigenlines.
The chosen affinoid V is reduced, as in the supplier’s eigencurve neighbourhood. Analytic equality at points alone detects only the reduction if nilpotents are present.
proofSteps: Two analytic functions on the reduced curve V agreeing on a Zariski-dense set agree; classical non-critical points accumulate at x (classical weights k′ ≫ 0 near k have v_p(β′) = v_p(β) < k′ + 1 on V).

At p=5 also certify the reported positive ordinary μ-invariant in the stated period normalization. These are computational targets, not proved numerical assertions. For the CM form of X₀(32) at split p=5, decency and θ-criticality do prove that the primary signed eigenline is one-dimensional and specializes to zero; a nonzero classical eigenvector has no eigenlift.

nodes.title: p-adic L-functions with a tame twist (Pollack §2.2–2.3)
nodes.statement: Let f be a newform of weight k + 2, level N and character ε, p ∤ N, and (f, α) a refinement of slope h < k + 1. Let M ≥ 1 be prime to p and Z_{p,M}^× = lim_n (Z/p^nM)^×. For n≥1 and (a, Mp)=1, the formula μ^±_{f,α}(P, a + p^nMZ_{p,M}) = α^{−n}λ^±(f, P; a, p^nM) − ε(p)p^kα^{−n−1}λ^±(f, P; a, p^{n−1}M) defines an h-admissible distribution on Z_{p,M}^× (Proposition 2.8); the n=0 values are obtained by finite additivity from n=1. It is a bounded measure only when h=0. Here λ^± are the modular symbols of f divided by periods Ω^±_f, and P runs over integral polynomials of degree ≤ k. For a tame character ψ, the power series L_p(f, α, ψ, T) = ∫ ψχ_u dμ^{sgn ψ}_{f,α} (u = 1 + T, χ_u the wild character with γ ↦ u) lies in K(α, ψ)[[T]] and is O(log_p(1 + T)^h). Take χ = x_p^jϕ with 0 ≤ j ≤ k and ϕ of finite order and conductor m = p^νM. Then L_p(f, α, χ) = e_p(α, χ)·m^{j+1}/(−2πi)^j·j!/τ(ϕ^{−1})·L(fϕ^{−1}, j + 1)/Ω^±_f, with e_p(α, χ) = α^{−ν}(1 − ϕ^{−1}(p)ε(p)p^{k−j}/α)(1 − ϕ(p)p^j/α). It is the unique O(log_p(1 + T)^h) function with these values (Proposition 2.11). With M = 1 it is the L_p(f, α) of L2/p-adic-l-function, up to the normalisation of periods.
hypotheses: Weights follow this roadmap: f has weight k + 2 (Pollack's k is our k + 2).
Analyticity and the growth O(log_p(1 + T)^h) are Višik's and Amice–Vélu's theorem (Pollack Theorem 2.6), as in L2/eigensymbol-admissibility.
The proof of the interpolation formula is Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum §14, which is not read; the formula agrees with L2/interpolation-and-uniqueness for M = 1 and with L4/euler-factor-comparison.

The term p^{n−1}M in the local formula requires n≥1. Torsion components use μ_{p−1} at odd p and μ₂ at p=2, with γ in 1+4Z₂ in the latter case; include the prime-to-p M-component of each tame character.
proofSteps: Additivity of μ^±_{f,α} is the T_p-eigenform relation; its growth is Višik's Lemma 3.8 (Proposition 2.8).
Integrate ψχ_u against μ^{sgn ψ} to get an analytic function of u in the open unit disc, O(log^h) by Theorem 2.6.

Evaluate at χ = x_p^jϕ with the twisted Mellin formula (L1/twisted-mellin-formula) to get Proposition 2.11. Uniqueness holds because a difference vanishes at all γ^jζ − 1 (0 ≤ j ≤ k) and is O(log^h) with h < k + 1.
acceptance: M = 1, ψ trivial: L2/p-adic-l-function.
ν = 0: both Euler factors appear; ν ≥ 1: only the prefactor α^{−ν}.

nodes.title: Both refinements at a good supersingular prime, and their zeros (Pollack §3)
nodes.statement: Let p ∤ NM be supersingular for f, so v_p(a_p) > 0. Then both roots α₁, α₂ of X² − a_pX + ε(p)p^{k+1} have slope h_i ∈ (0, k + 1), since h₁ + h₂ = k + 1. So both refinements are small slope, and both L_p(f, α_i, ψ, T) exist. (Mazur, Theorem 3.3) If h₁ ≠ h₂, at least one of them has infinitely many zeros in the open unit disc. (Perrin-Riou, Theorem 3.5) If a_p = 0, then h₁ = h₂ = (k + 1)/2 and α₂ = −α₁. Write L_p(f, α₁, ψ, T) = G⁺_ψ(T) + G⁻_ψ(T)·α₁ with G^± ∈ K(ψ)[[T]]. For odd p, G⁺_ψ vanishes at ζ_{p^{2n}} − 1 and G⁻_ψ at ζ_{p^{2n−1}} − 1 for n ≥ 1; for p = 2 the parities are reversed. One of the two L-functions has infinitely many zeros, and both do if α₁ ∉ K(ψ). (Corollary 3.6) For an elliptic curve E/Q with good supersingular reduction at p, one of the two has infinitely many zeros. For p ≥ 5, a_p = 0, because p | a_p and a_p² < 4p. For p = 2 or 3 with a_p ≠ 0, α₁/α₂ is a primitive fourth or sixth root of unity, which still forces G^± to have infinitely many zeros.
hypotheses: Weights follow this roadmap: f has weight k + 2 (Pollack's k is our k + 2).
A nonzero power series convergent on the open unit disc has finitely many zeros exactly when its coefficients are bounded (Lemma 3.2, Lazard).
proofSteps: Remark 2.12: L_p(f, α_i, ψ, ζ_{p^n} − 1) = c_n/α_i^{n+1} with c_n independent of α_i (exponent n + 2 for p = 2).
h₁ ≠ h₂: if both had finitely many zeros they would have bounded coefficients, and comparing valuations of α₁^{n+1}L(α₁) = α₂^{n+1}L(α₂) as n → ∞ contradicts h₁ ≠ h₂.

a_p = 0: α₁ = −α₂ makes the two values agree for odd n and differ by a sign for even n, which forces the zeros of G^±. Bounded G^± cannot have infinitely many zeros, so one L-function is unbounded, hence has infinitely many zeros.
acceptance: Ordinary p is excluded: then only one root has slope < k + 1.
Weight 2 (k = 0) with a_p = 0: both slopes are 1/2.
