nodes.title: Pollack's half-logarithms log^±_p (§4)
nodes.statement: Let γ generate 1 + qZ_p (q = p, or 4 if p = 2) and Φ_n(T) = Σ_{t=0}^{p−1} T^{p^{n−1}t}, the p^n-th cyclotomic polynomial. For an integer j put log⁺_{p,j}(T) = (1/p)·∏_{n≥1} Φ_{2n}(γ^{−j}(1 + T))/p and log⁻_{p,j}(T) = (1/p)·∏_{n≥1} Φ_{2n−1}(γ^{−j}(1 + T))/p. They converge on the open unit disc, and their zeros are exactly γ^jζ_{p^{2n}} − 1 (resp. γ^jζ_{p^{2n−1}} − 1), n ≥ 1, all simple (Lemma 4.1). Put log^±_p = ∏_{j=0}^{k} log^±_{p,j} (Corollary 4.2). Then, with u = γ^{−j}(1+T), p²(u−1)log⁺_{p,j}(T)log⁻_{p,j}(T) = log_p(u). At u=1 the analytic quotient log_p(u)/(u−1) has value 1, and both individual half-logarithms have value 1/p. The total weight-k products have logarithmic growth (k+1)/2 (Lemma 4.5). For k=0 inversion has the unit factors log⁺_p((1+T)⁻¹−1)=(1+T)^{p/(p+1)}log⁺_p(T) and log⁻_p((1+T)⁻¹−1)=(1+T)^{1/(p+1)}log⁻_p(T), interpreted by their convergent p-adic binomial series. This corrects Pollack Lemma 4.6, as in Sprung Lemma 4.26. For a primitive p^n-th root ζ, log⁺_p(ζ−1) vanishes for even n and equals p^{−(n+1)/2}∏_{j=1}^{(n−1)/2}Φ_{2j}(ζ) for odd n; log⁻_p(ζ−1) vanishes for odd n and equals p^{−n/2−1}∏_{j=1}^{n/2}Φ_{2j−1}(ζ) for even n (Lemma 4.7).
hypotheses: Weights follow this roadmap: f has weight k + 2 (Pollack's k is our k + 2). Pollack's product runs over 0 ≤ j ≤ k − 2 in his weight k.
For p = 2 the roles of log⁺ and log⁻ are exchanged in the decomposition (L4/plus-minus-decomposition).
proofSteps: Convergence: (1/p)Φ_{2n}(γ^{−j}(1 + T)) − 1 is divisible by (γ^{−j}(1 + T))^{p^{2n−1}} − 1, which tends to 0 (Lemma 4.1).
Zeros: log_p(γ^{−j}(1 + T)) = (γ^{−j}(1 + T) − 1)·lim_n ∏_{m≤n}Φ_m(γ^{−j}(1 + T))/p has simple zeros exactly at γ^jζ_{p^n} − 1, which gives Corollary 4.3 and the zero sets.

Growth is obtained from cyclotomic Gauss norms near radius one, with degree p^{n−1}(p−1) in the exponent, then multiplying the k+1 translated factors. No formula linear in the radius divided by that degree is used.
Values: Φ_m(ζ_{p^n}) = p for m > n, so only the head of each product survives (Lemma 4.7).

For inversion use Φ_m(u⁻¹)=u^{−p^{m−1}(p−1)}Φ_m(u). The sums of even and odd cyclotomic degrees converge p-adically to −p/(p+1) and −1/(p+1); their negatives give the two unit exponents. For p=2 the exponent 1/3 is still integral in ℤ₂; Sprung records the extra first factor in his convention.
acceptance: k = 0: p²·T·log⁺_p·log⁻_p = log_p(1 + T).
The leading 1/p is needed for the value p^{−(n+1)/2} of Lemma 4.7.

nodes.title: Pollack's ± decomposition of the supersingular p-adic L-function (Theorems 5.1 and 5.6)
nodes.statement: Let p ∤ NM with a_p = 0, and α a root of X² + ε(p)p^{k+1}. If p is odd, L_p(f, α, ψ, T) = L⁺_p(f, ψ, T)·log⁺_p(T) + L⁻_p(f, ψ, T)·log⁻_p(T)·α, with L^±_p(f, ψ, T) ∈ Λ_ψ ⊗ K_ψ (Λ_ψ = O_ψ[[T]]). They have bounded coefficients; every nonzero component has finitely many zeros. If p = 2, L₂(f, α, ψ, T) = L⁺₂·log⁻₂ + L⁻₂·log⁺₂·α with L^±₂ ∈ Λ_ψ ⊗ K_ψ (Theorem 5.1). For an elliptic curve E/Q with a_p = 0 and the periods Ω^±_E of §5.2.1, L^±_p(E, T) ∈ Z_p[[T]] for odd p. For p = 2, L₂(E, α, T) = L⁺₂(E, T)·log⁻₂(T) + L⁻₂(E, T)·(1/2)log⁺₂(T)·α with L^±₂(E, T) ∈ Z₂[[T]]; the factor 1/2 is needed for integrality (Theorem 5.6, Remark 5.7).
hypotheses: Weights follow this roadmap: f has weight k + 2 (Pollack's k is our k + 2).
The integrality in Theorem 5.6 uses that the Manin constant of E is prime to a good supersingular p (Remark 5.5), so 2[a/p^n]^± ∈ Z_p.
The finite-zero conclusion applies only to a nonzero bounded power series, on each fixed tame branch. A zero component is permitted and has no finite-zero conclusion.
proofSteps: G^±_ψ vanish at every zero of log^±_p: at γ^jζ − 1 for 0 ≤ j ≤ k, by the interpolation property (L4/tame-twist-p-adic-l-function). So log^±_p divides G^±_ψ in A(K_ψ) (Lazard).
G^±_ψ is O(log_p(1 + T)^{(k+1)/2}) (Theorem 2.6), and log^±_p ∼ log_p(1 + T)^{(k+1)/2} (Lemma 4.5), so L^±_p = G^±/log^± is O(1).
A bounded analytic function on the open unit disc has bounded coefficients (Lemma 5.2).
For E: approximate by the Riemann sums (2), and count the powers of p in the denominators (Lemma 5.9).
acceptance: a_p ≠ 0 at a supersingular p (p = 2, 3) is not covered.
L^±_p are Iwasawa functions: finitely many zeros on a nonzero branch, and the λ^±, μ^± invariants of Pollack's Table 1 are defined.

nodes.title: Supersingular examples at level 11
nodes.statement: Let f = f_{11} be the newform of X₀(11) (k = 0), with q-expansion q∏_{n≥1}(1 − qⁿ)²(1 − q^{11n})². (i) At p = 2: a₂ = −2, so p = 2 is supersingular. The roots of X² + 2X + 2 are −1 ± i, of 2-adic valuation 1/2 < 1, so both refinements are small slope. α₁/α₂ = −i is a primitive fourth root of unity, so by Corollary 3.6 at least one of L₂(f, α_i, T) has infinitely many zeros. Theorem 5.1 does not apply, since a₂ ≠ 0. (ii) At p = 19 (and p = 29): a₁₉ = a₂₉ = 0. The roots ±√−19 of X² + 19 have slope 1/2 and do not lie in Q₁₉, so both L₁₉(f, α_i, T) have infinitely many zeros (Theorem 3.5). Theorem 5.6 gives L₁₉(E, α, T) = L⁺₁₉·log⁺₁₉ + L⁻₁₉·log⁻₁₉·α with L^±₁₉ ∈ Z₁₉[[T]]. (iii) Pollack's Table 1 lists λ^± and μ^± for quadratic twists of 32A at p = 3, where a₃ = 0.

The coefficients a₂ = −2, a₁₉ = a₂₉ = 0 come from the eta-product; they were computed from the product formula to q⁶⁰.

nodes.title: Rational separation of parabolic and boundary Hecke supports
nodes.statement: Let N ≥ 3 and k ≥ 0, H = H¹(Γ(N), V_k(ℚ)) and P = H¹_par(Γ(N), V_k(ℚ)). Let T be the ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(H) generated by the usual good-prime T_ℓ and scalar S_ℓ, for primes ℓ not dividing N, transported through the polynomial-coefficient dictionary. There exist A ∈ T and coprime polynomials F,G ∈ ℚ[X] such that F(A) vanishes on P and the image of G(A) lies in P, equivalently G(A) vanishes on H/P. These are annihilators, not just a statement about individual eigenvectors.
hypotheses: The finite-dimensional rational cohomology and parabolic subspace are those of the existing L0 nodes, with the connected full-level carrier Γ(N).
The usual cohomological Hecke normalization and its transport to the adjugate polynomial action must be proved; the full-level comparison is recorded as an open request.
proofSteps: In weight two use Elkik §III: choose a prime ℓ congruent to 1 modulo N; T_ℓ acts on the boundary quotient by ℓ+1, while every cusp-form eigenvalue has absolute value strictly smaller than ℓ+1. Elkik proves the strict bound by the Petersson norm triangle inequality and the Fourier-expansion obstruction to equality, without Deligne’s theorem.

Transport the cusp-form bound to parabolic cohomology through Eichler–Shimura. Cayley–Hamilton gives rational annihilators and the absence of a shared root gives their coprimality. The native Nat.exists_prime_gt_modEq_one supplies the congruence prime by its cyclotomic argument; it is not a statement about every good prime.

For k>0 use Shokurov Theorem 4.3 and Corollary 4.4, pp.638–641: at full level, T_ℓ acts on the boundary by 1+ℓ^{k+1} for primes ℓ≡1 mod N. His Fourier-coefficient bound excludes this eigenvalue on cusp forms for sufficiently large such ℓ. Transport to the dual cohomological coefficient model via the requested full-level dictionary. Set A=T_ℓ, G=X−(1+ℓ^{k+1}), and F equal to the characteristic polynomial on P. Cayley–Hamilton and spectral exclusion give exactly the two annihilator conditions and coprimality, with no assumption that H is semisimple.
acceptance: The conditions on F and G control generalized eigenspaces, so a nonsemisimple boundary extension is included.
In weight two the boundary scalar ℓ+1 and Elkik’s strict cusp bound imply that X−(ℓ+1) is coprime to the parabolic characteristic polynomial.
Annihilator separation is over ℚ. It gives no coprimality over ℤ at a congruence prime.

nodes.title: The rational Drinfeld–Manin splitting
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 3 and k ≥ 0 there is a unique ℚ-linear retraction s_N : H¹(Γ(N),V_k(ℚ)) → H¹_par(Γ(N),V_k(ℚ)) equivariant for the rational good Hecke algebra (usual T_ℓ and scalar S_ℓ, ℓ not dividing N). Its inclusion-composite is the rational parabolic projector. Under the requested coefficient/local-system comparison, take the direct sum over geometric components to obtain Nakamura’s s_N : H¹(Y(N)(ℂ),𝒱_{k+2/ℚ}) → H¹(X(N)(ℂ),j_*𝒱_{k+2/ℚ}). Rationalization precedes this construction; no integral splitting is asserted.
hypotheses: Nakamura’s weight is k+2 and his curve Y(N) has all geometric components, whereas the connected Betti prototype uses Γ(N).

The comparison between Nakamura’s dual symmetric-power local system and the packet’s adjugate action, including determinant twists and usual versus adjoint Hecke operators, is requested from the geometric supplier.

Higher-weight rational spectral separation is justified by Shokurov Theorem 4.3 and Corollaries 4.4–4.5, pp.638–641. The remaining gap is the full-level coefficient and Hecke dictionary to Nakamura’s local system, not an unread-source claim.
proofSteps: Take A,F,G from rational-hecke-separation and Bézout polynomials a,b with aF+bG=1. Set e=b(A)G(A). Its image lies in P and it restricts to the identity on P, since F(A) kills P. Native projection theory identifies ker(e) as a complement.
Every good Hecke generator commutes with A, hence with e. Restrict the codomain of e to P to define s_N. This supplies existence, retraction, equivariance and idempotence.
If t is another Hecke-equivariant retraction, it commutes with A and all its polynomials. Since F(A) kills P, t(1−e)=a(A)|_P F(A)|_P t=0, while t e=s_N. Therefore t=s_N.
For an endomorphism preserving P and commuting with the good Hecke algebra, its commutation with the same polynomial projector proves naturality.

After the requested geometric dictionary, the usual and adjoint Hecke actions are related by Nakamura Lemma 3.1, with T′_ℓ=ℓ^k T_ℓ S_ℓ⁻¹ and S′_ℓ=ℓ^(2k) S_ℓ⁻¹. Thus the projector commutes with both. The full-curve action of complex conjugation, and the Galois action after rational p-adic coefficient extension and Betti–étale comparison, must be transported through that dictionary; the suggested file does not claim to have these geometric carriers.
acceptance: At full level N=3 and weight two (k=0), X(3) has genus zero, the parabolic subspace is zero and drinfeldManin 3 0 is the zero linear map. Ordinary H¹ has dimension three, so the ordinary and parabolic spaces are not identified.
At full level N=6 and weight two, dim_ℚ H¹_par=2 and s_6 restricts to the identity on that subspace. This excludes the zero retraction.

For H=ℚ², P=ℚ×{0} and T(x,y)=(y,2y), the Bézout projector e=1−T/2 sends (0,1) to (−1/2,0), fixes (1,0), kills T(H), commutes with T and satisfies e²=e. Projection onto the first coordinate alone fails to commute with T.
For the same model over ℤ there is no ℤ-linear retraction s:ℤ²→ℤ with s(1,0)=1 and s(Tv)=0 for all v: substituting v=(0,1) forces 1+2s(0,1)=0.

nodes.title: Coefficient embeddings and conjugate period coordinates
nodes.statement: For a normalized newform f of weight k+2, let E contain its coefficients and character values and let σ:E→E′ be a field embedding. The coefficient transport map on polynomial-valued symbols carries each signed f-eigenline to the signed f^σ-eigenline. With the transported basis φ^σ, period-normalized critical values transport by σ, including Gauss sums and the inverse twisting character. For p-adic constructions choose a p-adic place of E and the transported place of E′. An isometric extension σ_p of σ carries a refinement α to σ_p(α), preserves its slope, transports its normalized eigenlift and its p-adic L-function by coefficientwise transport. For small slope the equality follows from the control theorem or interpolation uniqueness; for critical slope it follows from the chosen family/eigenlift comparison, not interpolation alone. No transport of transcendental complex periods by σ is asserted.
hypotheses: The modular-form rational structure and construction of f^σ are imported from current ModularForms Layer 8G (Galois stability, character field, rationality), built on Layer 8. This packet transports the symbol coordinates and eigenlifts; it does not re-plan coefficient-field Galois stability.
The transport includes character values and the chosen signed basis. Unrelated choices of complex periods change the result by a coefficient-field unit.
Slope preservation requires an isometric map of the specified p-adic completions. Conjugating to a different place can change ordinarity.
proofSteps: Use symbols-base-change and the coefficient transport of the Hecke and diamond operators to identify the eigenspaces.
Apply the twisted Mellin formula to the transported symbol coordinates; the normalized values are algebraic.
Transport specialisation and U_p; small-slope lift uniqueness gives equality of distributions. The critical case imports the family comparison principle.

nodes.title: Euler depletion and primitive/imprimitive comparison
nodes.statement: Let f be a normalized newform of weight k+2 and level N, fix a nonzero refinement at p, and let ℓ≠p be prime. Put V_ℓf(z)=f(ℓz). If ℓ∤N define f^[ℓ]=f−a_ℓV_ℓf+ε(ℓ)ℓ^{k+1}V_{ℓ²}f, after raising every term to level Nℓ²; if ℓ|N define f^[ℓ]=f−a_ℓV_ℓf at level Nℓ. Its coefficients are a_n(f) for ℓ∤n and zero for ℓ|n. On distributions define [u]μ(g)=μ(z↦g(uz)). The good-prime deletion operator is E_ℓμ=μ−(a_ℓ/ℓ)[ℓ⁻¹]μ+ε(ℓ)ℓ^{k−1}[ℓ⁻²]μ; at a bad prime omit the quadratic term. Evaluated at χ(z)z^j it multiplies by 1−a_ℓχ(ℓ)⁻¹ℓ^{−j−1}+ε(ℓ)χ(ℓ)⁻²ℓ^{k−2j−1}, respectively 1−a_ℓχ(ℓ)⁻¹ℓ^{−j−1}. These are exactly the factors deleting the ℓ-Euler factor of L(fχ⁻¹,j+1). Compatible signed symbol bases give L_p(f^[ℓ],α)=E_ℓL_p(f,α) for slope<k+1. Depletion at several primes is the product of commuting E_ℓ.
hypotheses: χ(ℓ) is evaluated on a p-adic unit; ℓ=p is excluded.
ε(ℓ)=0 at a ramified prime and the newform relation at ℓ|N is a_{ℓn}=a_ℓa_n.
The depleted form is an eigenform for U_p and primes away from Npℓ; it need not be a newform. Its period coordinate is transported from f, not independently normalized.
Critical-slope equality requires compatible chosen eigenlifts or the family comparison; interpolation uniqueness is not used there.
proofSteps: Use Tau Ceti’s levelRaise coefficient formula and good/bad coefficient recurrences to prove the exact depletion formula.
Evaluate scaling on χ(z)z^j: [u] acts by χ(u)u^j. This gives the Euler polynomial, including both powers of ℓ.
U_p commutes with V_ℓ for ℓ≠p. Match the normalized interpolation values and invoke small-slope uniqueness.
acceptance: k=0 and χ=1: E_ℓ evaluates as 1−a_ℓ/ℓ+ε(ℓ)/ℓ.
k=0 at ℓ|N: the factor is 1−a_ℓ/ℓ, with no quadratic term.
The coefficient at ℓ and at ℓ² is zero, whereas the coefficient at 1 remains 1.
The scaling construction requires ℓ to be a p-adic unit. Taking ℓ=p fails this requirement.
